_about: Curated seed list: places you'd centre a ski trip around. Edit freely. category: resort | freeride | touring. level (resort only): all | advanced. tags: daytour (human-powered from a base), novelty (go for the place), heli, cat, boat, huts, volcano, spring, expedition, park. season/best are month numbers (season [start,end] may wrap the year). refElev = elevation (m) used for snow modelling. crowds 1 (empty) - 5 (lines). advisory = travel-advisory warning shown in the app. cost 1-5 = rough all-in cost per day for the usual way people do it (1 <$150, 2 $150-300, 3 $300-600, 4 $600-1,200, 5 $1,200+/day or $10k+ trips); self-guided touring is rated self-guided. pass = multi-resort pass affiliation, changes yearly: verify before relying on it. zone = map grouping (see zones); macro = world-view grouping.

destinations.name: Whistler Blackcomb
destinations.crowdNote: Huge terrain absorbs people, but village-gondola queues and the Sea-to-Sky drive get busy on weekends/holidays.
destinations.pitch: North America's biggest ski area: two mountains, 3,300+ ha, glaciers on top, rain risk at the base.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime: storm slabs and wind slabs dominate; generally fewer persistent layers than the interior.
destinations.weather: Wet, mild coastal storms; freezing levels can spike.

children.name: Spearhead Traverse
children.note: Classic hut-to-hut traverse through the glaciers behind Whistler and Blackcomb, starting from the lifts.
children.more: Usually done over two to three days, with huts along the way. Glacier travel skills or a guide are needed.

children.name: Duffey Lake Road · Joffre Lakes
children.note: Roadside touring an hour north of Pemberton, in a colder, drier snowpack.
children.more: Big peaks and couloirs right off Highway 99, popular with Vancouver ski tourers.

children.name: Garibaldi Park · Elfin Lakes
children.note: Hut-based touring in Garibaldi Provincial Park, reached from Squamish.
children.more: A long approach to the Elfin Lakes shelter opens up the Mamquam Icefield and peaks around Diamond Head.

tours.name: Spearhead Traverse
tours.note: The local classic: a multi-day glacier traverse from Blackcomb to Whistler.

tours.name: Joffre Peak and the Joffre Lakes area
tours.note: Big alpine objectives above the Duffey Lake Road.

tours.name: Mamquam Icefield
tours.note: Glacier touring from the Elfin Lakes shelter.

destinations.name: Lake Tahoe
destinations.crowdNote: Bay Area weekend crowds: Palisades lift lines and I-80 traffic on powder days are notorious. Go midweek.
destinations.pitch: A cluster of big resorts around the lake: huge snowfall years, sunny between storms, and very variable from season to season.
destinations.avalanche: Sierra maritime: big storm cycles, mostly storm/wind slabs; usually stabilises quickly.
destinations.weather: Feast-or-famine: atmospheric rivers bring metres of 'Sierra cement', then long sunny dry spells.

children.name: Palisades Tahoe (+ Alpine Meadows)
children.note: Steep, famous terrain (KT-22), Ikon. Busiest.

children.name: Northstar
children.note: Groomers and family, Epic.

children.name: Sugar Bowl
children.note: Highest snowfall at the crest, less busy.

children.name: Heavenly
children.note: South Lake, lake views, nightlife, Epic.

children.name: Kirkwood
children.note: Remote, steep, deep. Advanced skiers' choice, Epic.

children.name: Mt Rose
children.note: High base, close to Reno, the Chutes.

children.name: Donner Summit
children.note: Easy-access touring along I-80, with the Sierra Club's Peter Grubb Hut nearby.
children.more: Short tours, gentle and steep terrain, and quick escapes on storm days.

children.name: Carson Pass
children.note: High-elevation touring south of the lake, a classic for spring corn.
children.more: Round Top and the Sisters are popular objectives.

children.name: Mt Rose backcountry
children.note: Highland touring above Reno, with easy road access.
children.more: Tamarack Peak is a well-known local tour.

children.name: Desolation Wilderness
children.note: Granite wilderness above Emerald Bay, with big lines in a wild setting.
children.more: Longer approaches; Jake's Peak and Maggie's Peaks are popular from Highway 89.

tours.name: Round Top
tours.note: The classic Carson Pass objective, with couloirs and big spring descents.

tours.name: Tamarack Peak
tours.note: Popular, accessible bowls near the top of the Mt Rose highway.

tours.name: Jake's Peak
tours.note: Steep trees and views over Emerald Bay.

tours.name: Castle Peak
tours.note: A well-known tour from Donner Summit.

destinations.name: Mammoth Mountain
destinations.crowdNote: LA weekend crowds; midweek is quiet.
destinations.pitch: High-altitude volcano with one of the longest seasons in the US, often into June.
destinations.avalanche: Sierra maritime/transitional: big storm cycles bring storm and wind slabs that usually settle within days; wet slides in spring.
destinations.weather: Big storms then intense sun; wind is a factor at the top.

children.name: Mammoth Mountain
children.note: Main mountain.

children.name: June Mountain
children.note: Small, steep, uncrowded sister hill.

destinations.name: Cottonwood Canyons (Alta, Snowbird, Brighton, Solitude)
destinations.crowdNote: Snow is legendary but the canyon road is a parking lot on powder mornings (the 'Red Snake'). Interlodge closures happen.
destinations.pitch: 'Greatest Snow on Earth': light, frequent lake-effect snow and steep terrain, 40 minutes from a major airport.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain: often a buried persistent weak layer from early-season facets.
destinations.weather: Frequent cold storms; dry, light snow.

children.name: Alta
children.note: Skiers only, classic steeps.

children.name: Snowbird
children.note: Big, steep, tram. Long season.

children.name: Brighton
children.note: Locals' hill, night skiing.

children.name: Solitude
children.note: Quieter, Honeycomb Canyon.

children.name: White Pine trailhead
children.note: Little Cottonwood trailhead to White Pine, Red Pine and Maybird.
children.more: A popular starting point for tours on the south side of the canyon.

children.name: Mount Superior
children.note: Iconic steep south face above Little Cottonwood, toured from the road.
children.more: One of the Wasatch's most recognisable ski lines; a serious objective in avalanche terms.

children.name: Grizzly Gulch
children.note: Easy-access tours from the top of Little Cottonwood, near Alta.
children.more: A good first tour for visitors, leading toward Twin Lakes Pass and Big Cottonwood.

children.name: Mill D & Cardiff Fork
children.note: Big Cottonwood trailheads to Cardiff Fork, Days Fork and Mill D.
children.more: Long drainages with classic bowls and trees.

tours.name: Mount Superior South Face
tours.note: The famous line above Little Cottonwood.

tours.name: Grizzly Gulch
tours.note: Gentle, popular tours near Alta.

tours.name: Cardiff Fork
tours.note: Big bowls and chutes reached from Big Cottonwood.

tours.name: Days Fork
tours.note: Classic bowls with a long exit.

tours.name: White Pine and Red Pine
tours.note: Long approaches to quieter terrain.

destinations.name: Park City & Deer Valley
destinations.crowdNote: Big but busy, especially holidays.
destinations.pitch: The US's largest single resort plus Deer Valley's luxury groomers; a real town with food and nightlife. Family-friendly.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain: early-season facets can leave a buried persistent weak layer; the backcountry gates off the resorts see serious slides.
destinations.weather: Less snow than the Cottonwoods; sunny.

children.name: Park City Mountain
children.note: Biggest US resort, Epic.

children.name: Deer Valley
children.note: Skiers only, luxury, Ikon.

children.name: Guardsman Pass
children.note: Backcountry access on the ridge between Park City and Big Cottonwood.
children.more: The road is only partly open in winter; check access before planning a tour.

destinations.name: Jackson Hole
destinations.crowdNote: Tram line on powder days; otherwise manageable.
destinations.pitch: Steep, big-vertical resort with Corbet's Couloir and world-class sidecountry; Grand Targhee next door for deep snow.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain/continental: persistent slabs are common in the Tetons.
destinations.weather: Cold; storms off the Pacific, deep at Targhee.

children.name: Jackson Hole Mountain Resort
children.note: Steeps, tram, Corbet's.

children.name: Grand Targhee
children.note: West side of the Tetons: deeper, cheaper, mellow.

destinations.name: Big Sky
destinations.crowdNote: Lots of acres per skier.
destinations.pitch: Huge, uncrowded terrain under Lone Peak's steep tram line.
destinations.avalanche: Continental: cold, shallow snowpack with persistent weak layers.
destinations.weather: Cold, drier snow, windy summit.

children.name: Lone Peak tram
children.note: The summit of Big Sky, with steep, exposed lines like the Big Couloir.

children.name: Bridger Bowl
children.note: Community-run hill near Bozeman, famous for the hike-to steeps of the Ridge.

children.name: Cooke City
children.note: Remote town near Yellowstone's northeast gate, known for deep snow and snowmobile-accessed backcountry.
children.more: The road from the east closes in winter; access is through Yellowstone from Gardiner.

tours.name: The Big Couloir
tours.note: Big Sky's signature line, off the top of Lone Peak (patrol check-in required).

tours.name: The Ridge at Bridger Bowl
tours.note: Hike-to chutes and cliffs above the lifts (avalanche gear required).

tours.name: Hyalite Canyon
tours.note: Bozeman's local backcountry, better known for ice climbing but with touring too.

destinations.name: Aspen Snowmass
destinations.crowdNote: Four mountains spread people out.
destinations.pitch: Four mountains (Snowmass, Ajax, Highlands, Buttermilk) and a glamorous town; Highland Bowl hike for experts.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: deep persistent slabs a recurring theme.
destinations.weather: Sunny, cold, dry snow.

children.name: Aspen Mountain (Ajax)
children.note: Steep groomers above town, no beginner terrain.

children.name: Snowmass
children.note: Biggest; family hub.

children.name: Aspen Highlands
children.note: Highland Bowl hike-to expert terrain.

children.name: Buttermilk
children.note: Beginners and X Games park.

children.name: Highland Bowl
children.note: Hike-to inbounds bowl at Aspen Highlands, with steep open faces up to about 3,780 m.

tours.name: Highland Bowl
tours.note: Hike from the top of Aspen Highlands' Loge Peak lift to the summit of the bowl.

tours.name: Independence Pass in spring
tours.note: Corn-skiing on the high peaks once the pass road opens, usually in late May.

destinations.name: Vail & Beaver Creek
destinations.crowdNote: Front Range I-70 crowds and weekend lines.
destinations.pitch: Massive groomed front side plus the Back Bowls; polished, expensive resort villages.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: cold, shallow early snowpack builds facets, so deep persistent slabs are a recurring winter-long problem off-piste.
destinations.weather: Sunny, cold, light snow.

children.name: Vail
children.note: Front side plus the Back Bowls.

children.name: Beaver Creek
children.note: Upscale, quieter, Birds of Prey.

children.name: Vail Pass
children.note: Popular backcountry and snowmobile area right off I-70, east of Vail.
children.more: A recreation fee applies in winter. Shrine Pass is a gentle classic from here.

tours.name: Shrine Pass
tours.note: A gentle, scenic tour from Vail Pass toward Red Cliff.

destinations.name: Summit County (Breckenridge, Keystone, A-Basin, Copper)
destinations.crowdNote: Closest big resorts to Denver: heavy weekend traffic.
destinations.pitch: High-altitude cluster with lots of choice; A-Basin skis into June.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: weak, faceted base layers are common and persistent slabs can stay reactive all season outside the resorts.
destinations.weather: High, cold, windy at the top, sunny.

children.name: Breckenridge
children.note: Epic. Big, town vibe.

children.name: Keystone
children.note: Epic. Night skiing, family.

children.name: Arapahoe Basin
children.note: High, steep, long season.

children.name: Copper Mountain
children.note: Ikon. Naturally split by ability.

children.name: Loveland Ski Area
children.note: No-frills locals' hill on the Continental Divide, with free cat rides to the ridge.

children.name: Loveland Pass
children.note: Famous road-accessed backcountry on the Divide, often skied in short laps.
children.more: Easy access hides serious avalanche terrain. The road closes in storms.

children.name: Berthoud Pass
children.note: Former ski area turned popular backcountry, above Winter Park.
children.more: Lots of terrain on both sides of the highway, from gentle to steep.

tours.name: Loveland Pass laps
tours.note: Short runs off the pass, back to the road.

tours.name: Berthoud Pass east and west sides
tours.note: Classic local backcountry with options for every condition.

destinations.name: Steamboat
destinations.pitch: 'Champagne powder' and famous tree skiing; ranch-town feel.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental, though wetter than most of the state: persistent weak layers still form in thin early winters.
destinations.weather: Frequent light snowfall, cold.

children.name: Steamboat Resort
children.note: The main mountain: glades, Champagne Powder and the new Fish Creek Canyon terrain.

children.name: Howelsen Hill
children.note: Historic town hill with ski jumps and night skiing, operating since 1915.

children.name: Buffalo Pass
children.note: One of the snowiest places in Colorado, with cat skiing and touring.
children.more: The road is a snowmobile route in winter; access takes planning.

children.name: Rabbit Ears Pass
children.note: Gentle, road-accessed touring on the highway to Denver.

tours.name: Buffalo Pass tours
tours.note: Deep-snow tree and meadow skiing north of town.

tours.name: Rabbit Ears Pass
tours.note: Mellow touring and good for beginners to the backcountry.

destinations.name: Telluride
destinations.crowdNote: Remote: rarely a line.
destinations.pitch: Stunning box canyon town with a mix of family groomers and hike-to expert terrain.
destinations.avalanche: San Juan continental: some of the weakest snowpacks in the US.
destinations.weather: Sunny, dry, cold.

children.name: Telluride Ski Resort
children.note: Groomers, bumps and hike-to steeps above the box canyon.

children.name: Palmyra Peak
children.note: Hike-to expert terrain at the top of the resort, at about 4,000 m.

children.name: Lizard Head Pass
children.note: Classic San Juan backcountry about 30 minutes south of town.
children.more: Black Face is the well-known tour; the snowpack is often weak.

tours.name: Palmyra Peak
tours.note: The resort's highest hike-to terrain.

tours.name: Black Face
tours.note: Popular tour from Lizard Head Pass.

destinations.name: Crested Butte
destinations.pitch: Funky old mining town; the Extreme Limits are among the steepest lift-served terrain in the US.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: shallow, faceted snowpack with persistent slabs; the Elk Mountains have a serious avalanche history.
destinations.weather: Cold, sunny.

children.name: Crested Butte Mountain Resort
children.note: Groomers below, the steep Extreme Limits above.

children.name: Kebler Pass & Mount Emmons
children.note: Classic backcountry west of town, including the Red Lady Bowl.
children.more: The road is closed to cars in winter beyond the trailhead.

children.name: Snodgrass Mountain
children.note: Short, popular tours next to the ski area.

tours.name: Red Lady Bowl
tours.note: The big bowl on Mount Emmons, visible from town.

tours.name: Snodgrass Mountain
tours.note: A quick tour with good views.

destinations.name: Taos Ski Valley
destinations.pitch: Steep, high, sunny; hike-to Kachina and Highline ridges. Adobe culture.
destinations.avalanche: Southern Rockies continental: often thin and faceted, with persistent slabs; dry spells between storms weaken the snowpack further.
destinations.weather: Southwestern sun, variable snow years.

children.name: Taos Ski Valley
children.note: Steep inbounds terrain, ski-school traditions and a small European-style village.

children.name: Kachina Peak & Highline Ridge
children.note: The highest lift and the hike-to ridges with the resort's steepest chutes.

children.name: Wheeler Peak
children.note: New Mexico's highest summit, a spring tour above the ski valley.

tours.name: Highline Ridge chutes
tours.note: Hike-to steeps reached from the top of Lift 2.

tours.name: Wheeler Peak
tours.note: Long spring tour to the top of New Mexico.

destinations.name: Sun Valley
destinations.pitch: America's first destination resort: long consistent fall-line groomers on Bald Mountain.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain: a mix of storm slabs and persistent weak layers; the backcountry around Ketchum is forecast by the Sawtooth center.
destinations.weather: Sunny, modest snowfall.

children.name: Bald Mountain
children.note: Baldy: 1,000 m of steady fall-line skiing and famous grooming.

children.name: Dollar Mountain
children.note: Gentle learning hill and terrain parks next to the village.

children.name: Galena Summit
children.note: Local road-accessed touring on the highway north toward Stanley.

children.name: Sawtooths · Stanley
children.note: Wild granite range with yurt-based touring.
children.more: Remote and very cold in midwinter; most trips are guided.

tours.name: Galena Summit tours
tours.note: Accessible terrain on both sides of the pass.

tours.name: Sawtooth yurt trips
tours.note: Multi-day touring from backcountry yurts.

destinations.name: Alyeska
destinations.pitch: Sea-level base and steep upper bowls; pairs with Turnagain Pass touring and Chugach heli.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal Alaska maritime: heavy storms and strong winds build deep storm and wind slabs; short days, rain-on-snow events possible.
destinations.weather: Short days midwinter, wet coastal storms.

children.name: Alyeska Resort
children.note: Tram-served steeps above Turnagain Arm.

children.name: Turnagain Pass
children.note: Classic roadside touring on the Seward Highway, 40 minutes south.
children.more: Motorized users are allowed on the west side (Seattle Ridge); the east side (Tincan, Sunburst) is non-motorized.

tours.name: Tincan
tours.note: The most popular Turnagain tour: trees, then open slopes.

tours.name: Sunburst
tours.note: Bigger, open slopes above the pass.

tours.name: Seattle Ridge
tours.note: West-side ridge with long, open runs; shared with snowmachines.

destinations.name: Hatcher Pass
destinations.crowdNote: Anchorage and Palmer locals on weekends.
destinations.pitch: Anchorage's other backyard: rocky Talkeetna peaks above an old gold mine, with a colder, drier snowpack than the coast.
destinations.avalanche: Transitional snowpack, colder and shallower than Turnagain, with persistent weak layers. The Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center forecasts the area.
destinations.weather: Cold and windy, with less snow than the coast but better preservation.

children.name: Independence Mine
children.note: Plowed access and the heart of the touring terrain.

destinations.name: Mt. Baker
destinations.crowdNote: Seattle weekends.
destinations.pitch: Record-holding snowfall, rustic lifts, and sidecountry and backcountry access off the top. Core skier culture.
destinations.avalanche: Cascade maritime: storm slabs, deep heavy snow.
destinations.weather: Very wet, heavy snow; often stormy.

children.name: Mt. Baker Ski Area
children.note: Record snowfall, steep natural terrain and old-school lifts.

children.name: Artist Point & Table Mountain
children.note: Popular touring at the top of the access road, with Baker and Shuksan views.

children.name: Shuksan Arm
children.note: Long ridge toward Mount Shuksan, reached from the ski area's backcountry gates.
children.more: Steep, committing descents; serious avalanche terrain.

tours.name: Shuksan Arm
tours.note: Classic steep descents from the ski area's gates.

tours.name: Table Mountain
tours.note: Short tours with big views.

destinations.name: Silverton Mountain
destinations.crowdNote: Guided-only days cap numbers.
destinations.pitch: One chairlift, all expert, avalanche-gear-required, mostly guided. Optional heli drops.
destinations.avalanche: San Juan continental: notoriously weak snowpack.
destinations.weather: High altitude, cold, sunny between storms.

destinations.name: Revelstoke
destinations.crowdNote: Getting busier, but still modest.
destinations.pitch: Biggest lift-served vertical in North America (1,713 m); hub for cat and heli skiing and Rogers Pass.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC transitional: buried surface hoar a classic problem.
destinations.weather: Deep, frequent snowfall, often cloudy.

children.name: Revelstoke Mountain Resort
children.note: The biggest lift-served vertical in North America.

children.name: Mount Revelstoke National Park
children.note: Touring above town from the Meadows in the Sky Parkway.

children.name: Mount Begbie
children.note: Glaciated peak across the valley from town, a classic spring objective.
children.more: A ski-mountaineering trip, with glacier travel.

tours.name: Mount Begbie
tours.note: Spring ski mountaineering with views over Revelstoke.

tours.name: Mount Revelstoke parkway tours
tours.note: Accessible touring in the national park above town.

destinations.name: Kicking Horse
destinations.pitch: Steep chutes and big bowls above Golden; on the Powder Highway with Revelstoke.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC/Rockies transitional: buried surface hoar and facets are common persistent layers, so off-piste needs care all season.
destinations.weather: Drier, colder than the coast.

destinations.name: Fernie
destinations.crowdNote: Calgary weekends.
destinations.pitch: Five big alpine bowls and lots of snow in a historic town.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC: big snowfall with buried surface hoar layers that can linger for weeks; storm slabs after each cycle.
destinations.weather: Big snowfall, mild by Rockies standards.

children.name: Fernie Alpine Resort
children.note: Five big bowls, deep snow and good trees.

children.name: Island Lake Lodge
children.note: Famous cat-skiing lodge in the next valley, in the Lizard Range.

destinations.name: Kootenays (Red Mountain & Whitewater)
destinations.crowdNote: Tiny crowds.
destinations.pitch: Old-school, steep tree skiing in Rossland and Nelson; lots of cat skiing nearby.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC: buried surface hoar and storm slabs are the classic problems; the slackcountry beyond the ropes is serious terrain.
destinations.weather: Frequent snow, often cloudy.

children.name: RED Mountain (Rossland)
children.note: Steep trees, two mountains, cat skiing.

children.name: Whitewater (Nelson)
children.note: Small, deep, great food, cool town.

children.name: Kootenay Pass
children.note: Classic road-accessed touring on Highway 3.
children.more: Busy on weekends. The highway closes for avalanche control.

tours.name: Ripple Ridge
tours.note: Popular, accessible tour at Kootenay Pass.

tours.name: Lightning Strike
tours.note: Steeper terrain off Kootenay Pass.

destinations.name: Banff (Lake Louise, Sunshine, Norquay)
destinations.pitch: Three resorts inside a national park; spectacular scenery, cold, long season.
destinations.avalanche: Rockies continental: weak, faceted base layers are typical.
destinations.weather: Cold (−20s °C), dry snow.

children.name: Lake Louise
children.note: Big, scenic.

children.name: Sunshine Village
children.note: Snowiest of the three; Delirium Dive.

children.name: Mt Norquay
children.note: Small, near town, night skiing.

children.name: Skoki Lodge
children.note: Historic backcountry lodge reached on skis from Lake Louise.
children.more: Built in the 1930s and still without road access. Book well ahead.

children.name: Bow Summit · Icefields Parkway
children.note: Road-accessed touring on the Icefields Parkway north of Lake Louise.
children.more: Gateway to the Wapta Icefield and many day tours.

tours.name: Skoki Lodge trip
tours.note: A classic multi-day trip to the historic lodge, with touring around it.

tours.name: Bow Summit tours
tours.note: Accessible alpine touring above the Parkway.

destinations.name: Big White
destinations.pitch: Family ski-in/ski-out village with dry 'champagne powder'; famous for fog (snow ghosts).
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC (Okanagan): lighter snowfall than the Kootenays, with surface hoar layers possible; mostly gentle in-bounds terrain.
destinations.weather: Often foggy, light snow.

children.name: Big White
children.note: Snow ghosts, light powder and Canada's biggest ski-in, ski-out village.

children.name: SilverStar
children.note: Colourful village near Vernon, with big cross-country trails.

children.name: Apex Mountain
children.note: Smaller, steeper hill near Penticton.

destinations.name: Mont-Tremblant
destinations.crowdNote: Holiday and weekend crowds from Montreal.
destinations.pitch: Eastern North America's flagship resort village with French-Canadian charm.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resort, avalanche risk is minimal (low-angle, treed eastern terrain). No regular avalanche forecast is needed here.
destinations.weather: Cold, icy days possible; freeze-thaw.

destinations.name: Northern Vermont (Stowe, Jay Peak, Sugarbush)
destinations.crowdNote: Holiday weekends busy.
destinations.pitch: Best snow in the US Northeast; classic New England tree skiing.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resorts, avalanche risk is minimal. Steeper slides and gullies (e.g. Smugglers' Notch) can avalanche after big storms.
destinations.weather: Cold, variable, icy spells.

children.name: Stowe
children.note: Epic. Classic, upscale.

children.name: Jay Peak
children.note: Most snow in the East, glades.

children.name: Sugarbush
children.note: Ikon. Two mountains.

children.name: Mad River Glen
children.note: Skiers-only co-op with a single chair.

children.name: Smugglers' Notch
children.note: Family resort with surprisingly steep terrain.

children.name: Brandon Gap
children.note: Community-cut backcountry glades in the Green Mountain National Forest.

destinations.name: Rogers Pass
destinations.crowdNote: Popular parking areas on sunny weekends; permit system (winter restricted areas).
destinations.airport: Calgary 4h / Kelowna 3h; base in Revelstoke or Golden
destinations.pitch: Iconic Selkirk backcountry on the Trans-Canada Highway: huge snowfall, glaciers, trees, and huts.
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC: buried surface hoar and deep persistent layers; Parks Canada forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Stormy and deep; clear spells bring cold.

children.name: Illecillewaet & Wheeler Hut
children.note: Trailhead at the Illecillewaet campground, with the ACC's Wheeler Hut. Gateway to the Illecillewaet Glacier and Asulkan valley.
children.more: The most-used starting point at the pass. The valley floor is gentle, then the terrain steepens quickly toward the glaciers and the peaks around Sir Donald.

children.name: Asulkan Valley
children.note: Long valley to the Asulkan Glacier and the ACC's Asulkan Cabin. Classic glacier and hut skiing.
children.more: A gradual approach up the valley leads to big glacier terrain, best done as an overnight from the Asulkan Cabin.

children.name: Illecillewaet Glacier
children.note: The big glacier below Sir Donald and the Perley Rock area. Multi-day and glacier objectives.
children.more: Glacier travel skills or a guide needed. Links toward the Bonney and Asulkan areas for longer trips.

children.name: Balu Pass & Connaught Creek
children.note: The most popular day-touring drainage, just west of the Discovery Centre: trees and open bowls on both sides.
children.more: Short approaches, lots of terrain choice, and good options in stormy weather. Check which areas are open each morning.

children.name: Bruins Pass
children.note: Higher terrain at the head of the Connaught drainage, with bigger alpine runs.

tours.name: Asulkan Valley to the Asulkan Cabin
tours.note: A classic overnight: valley approach, hut night, then glacier runs above the cabin.

tours.name: Balu Pass
tours.note: The standard first day at the pass, with tree skiing and alpine bowls either side.

tours.name: 8812 Bowl
tours.note: A popular big open bowl reached from the Connaught side.

tours.name: Ursus Minor and Ursus Major
tours.note: Steeper tree and alpine runs north of Balu Pass, favourites in good conditions.

tours.name: Bonney Glacier and Mount Bonney
tours.note: A longer, more committing glacier objective south of the pass.

destinations.name: Interior BC Heli & Cat (Selkirks, Monashees, Bugaboos)
destinations.crowdNote: Lodge-based, small groups.
destinations.airport: Calgary / Kelowna, plus heli or road transfer
destinations.pitch: The birthplace of heli-skiing: endless old-growth tree runs and glaciers from remote lodges (CMH, Mike Wiegele, Baldface cat).
destinations.avalanche: Interior BC; operators run professional programs.
destinations.weather: Deep, cold-smoke powder; flying days lost to cloud.

children.name: CMH Bugaboos
children.note: Original heli lodge.

children.name: Mike Wiegele (Blue River)
children.note: Monashees and Cariboos.

children.name: Baldface (cat)
children.note: Classic cat skiing near Nelson.

destinations.name: Teton Pass & Grand Teton backcountry
destinations.crowdNote: Teton Pass road-side is heavily used.
destinations.pitch: Road-accessed touring off Teton Pass; spring ski mountaineering in Grand Teton NP.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain/continental: persistent slabs are common and the terrain is big and close to the road; the Bridger-Teton center forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Cold, frequent snow.

children.name: Teton Pass
children.note: Road-accessed backcountry between Jackson and Victor.
children.more: Busy on good days; slopes above the highway are closed to skiing when they could threaten the road.

children.name: Grand Teton National Park
children.note: Serious spring ski mountaineering on the Grand, Moran, Owen and the South Teton.

children.name: Taggart Lake trailhead
children.note: Popular park-road trailhead for tours into the canyons.

tours.name: Glory Bowl
tours.note: The famous slide path above the highway at Teton Pass.

tours.name: Grand Teton descent
tours.note: A landmark American ski descent for highly experienced ski mountaineers.

destinations.name: Chugach / Valdez Heli
destinations.pitch: The steep spines of ski films. Coastal Alaska snow sticks to 50° faces. Very weather-dependent.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime; sluff management, wind slabs; deep instabilities possible.
destinations.weather: Down days are common: budget them in.

children.name: Thompson Pass
children.note: Heli base and roadside touring on the Richardson Highway.

children.name: Valdez
children.note: Port town and the base for most visitors.

destinations.name: Haines Heli
destinations.pitch: Alaska's other heli mecca: big glaciated lines, smaller and quieter than Valdez.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime: deep storm and wind slabs, big sluffs on steep faces; operators run professional avalanche programs.
destinations.weather: Very variable; down days.

children.name: Haines
children.note: Small town and heli base on the Inside Passage.

children.name: Chilkat Pass (Haines Highway)
children.note: Road-access touring near the Canadian border.

destinations.name: White Pass (Skagway–Yukon)
destinations.crowdNote: Locals from Whitehorse and Skagway.
destinations.airport: Whitehorse (YXY) 2 h / Juneau + ferry to Skagway
destinations.pitch: Roadside touring on a historic gold-rush pass, with sea-level fjords on one side and the Yukon on the other.
destinations.avalanche: Transitional to coastal snowpack. Avalanche Canada forecasts the White Pass area.
destinations.weather: Wind and storms off the coast; long spring days.

children.name: White Pass summit
children.note: Roadside alpine touring on the border.

children.name: Fraser
children.note: Customs post and touring terrain north of the pass.

destinations.name: Colorado Hut Systems (10th Mountain)
destinations.crowdNote: Huts book a year ahead via lottery.
destinations.pitch: Network of 30+ backcountry huts between Vail, Aspen and Leadville.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: deep persistent slabs. Conservative terrain choices matter.
destinations.weather: Cold, sunny, dry snow.

children.name: Shrine Mountain Inn
children.note: Hut near Vail Pass with easy access, popular with first-timers.

children.name: Uncle Bud's & Skinner huts
children.note: High huts near Leadville, with open terrain above the trees.

children.name: Margy's Hut
children.note: Classic hut above the Fryingpan Valley, between Aspen and Basalt.

tours.name: Shrine Mountain Inn
tours.note: An easy introduction to the hut system.

tours.name: Uncle Bud's to Skinner hut traverse
tours.note: A high traverse between two classic huts.

tours.name: Margy's Hut
tours.note: Long approach to a well-loved hut with good nearby terrain.

destinations.name: San Juans Backcountry (Red Mountain Pass)
destinations.pitch: High-alpine road-access touring between Silverton and Ouray, with yurts and huts.
destinations.avalanche: One of the weakest snowpacks anywhere: very conservative early season.
destinations.weather: High, cold, sunny.

children.name: Red Mountain Pass
children.note: The main road-accessed zone, with big terrain from 3,350 m.

children.name: Molas Pass
children.note: Gentler touring south of Silverton, with big views.

children.name: Ophir Pass
children.note: Steeper terrain on the old road between Silverton and Ophir.

tours.name: McMillan Peak
tours.note: Popular tour from the top of Red Mountain Pass.

tours.name: Red Mountain No. 3
tours.note: One of the classic Red Mountains above the pass.

destinations.name: Cascade Volcanoes (Hood, Adams, St. Helens, Rainier, Baker)
destinations.pitch: Spring corn-snow road trip, skiing big glaciated volcanoes from the summit.
destinations.avalanche: Spring snowpack: daily wet-snow cycles (start early, off before it softens), cornices, plus crevasses and icefall on the glaciers.
destinations.weather: Stable spring highs; storms off the Pacific.

children.name: Mount Hood · Timberline
children.note: South side of Hood from Timberline Lodge: the most accessible volcano ski in the Cascades.
children.more: Climb alongside the ski area, then above it toward Crater Rock. Spring corn and big views of Jefferson and the Sisters.

children.name: Mount Adams · South Climb
children.note: Broad south-side slopes and the famous Southwest Chutes, from the Cold Springs trailhead.
children.more: A long day on gentle terrain to the false summit, or a camp at Lunch Counter. The Southwest Chutes are a long, sustained descent for strong skiers.

children.name: Mount St. Helens · Marble Mountain
children.note: Spring climbs from the Marble Mountain Sno-Park to the crater rim.
children.more: Ski from the rim of the 1980 crater. A climbing permit is required, sold in limited numbers in spring.

children.name: Mount Rainier · Paradise
children.note: Paradise and the Muir Snowfield: a huge descent without glacier travel.
children.more: Camp Muir, at about 3,100 m, is the classic objective. Higher up, Rainier is a glaciated mountaineering climb.

children.name: Mount Baker · Heliotrope Ridge
children.note: North-side access to the Coleman and Deming glaciers.
children.more: Glaciated terrain from early on. The south side, from Schreiber's Meadow and the Easton Glacier, is the other popular route.

tours.name: Mount Hood South Side
tours.note: From Timberline toward Crater Rock and, for skilled parties, the summit.

tours.name: Southwest Chutes, Mount Adams
tours.note: Famous long gullies off the south side of Adams.

tours.name: Worm Flows, Mount St. Helens
tours.note: The standard winter and spring route to the crater rim.

tours.name: Muir Snowfield to Camp Muir
tours.note: A huge, non-glaciated descent on Rainier's south side.

tours.name: Easton Glacier, Mount Baker
tours.note: The popular south-side ski route on Baker.

destinations.name: Eastern Sierra Backcountry
destinations.pitch: Huge couloirs above Highway 395 (Bishop, June Lake, Mammoth); world-class spring corn.
destinations.avalanche: Sierra: big storms then stable; spring wet slides.
destinations.weather: Sunny, big storm cycles.

children.name: Rock Creek
children.note: High-elevation road access with gentle to big terrain.

children.name: Convict Lake
children.note: Under Mount Morrison and Laurel Mountain, with famous couloirs.

children.name: June Lake · Carson Peak
children.note: Big north-facing terrain above June Lake.

children.name: Tioga Pass · Mount Dana
children.note: High terrain near Yosemite's east entrance, once the road opens in late spring.

children.name: Mount Tom
children.note: The giant above Bishop, with long spring descents.

tours.name: Mendenhall Couloir, Laurel Mountain
tours.note: A famous steep line above Convict Lake.

tours.name: Dana Couloir
tours.note: Classic spring couloir near Tioga Pass.

tours.name: Mount Tom
tours.note: Huge spring descents above Bishop.

tours.name: Rock Creek tours
tours.note: Gentler high-elevation touring, good for a first day.

destinations.name: Mt Washington (Tuckerman Ravine)
destinations.crowdNote: Spring weekends are a scene.
destinations.pitch: Classic Eastern spring pilgrimage to the ravine headwall.
destinations.avalanche: Wind-loaded ravines; forecast by Mount Washington Avalanche Center.
destinations.weather: Notorious for extreme wind and weather.

children.name: Pinkham Notch
children.note: The trailhead and AMC base at the foot of the mountain.

children.name: Tuckerman Ravine
children.note: The famous bowl and headwall.

children.name: Gulf of Slides
children.note: A quieter bowl in the next valley south.

tours.name: The Headwall
tours.note: The famous steep face, around 50° near the top.

tours.name: Hillman's Highway
tours.note: The longest gully, a bit less steep.

tours.name: Left Gully
tours.note: A popular gully on the ravine's left side.

destinations.name: Chic-Chocs (Gaspésie)
destinations.airport: Montréal, then a long drive / Mont-Joli
destinations.pitch: Eastern Canada's best snow: open alpine bowls above the St. Lawrence, with huts and lodges.
destinations.avalanche: Wind slabs and cornices; Avalanche Québec forecasts.
destinations.weather: Maritime, windy, frequent snow.

children.name: Mont Albert
children.note: Flat-topped mountain with bowls on its flanks.

children.name: Mont Jacques-Cartier
children.note: Highest peak in southern Québec, in the caribou habitat.

children.name: Gîte du Mont-Albert
children.note: Park lodge and the main base for independent touring.

tours.name: Mont Albert bowls
tours.note: Open bowls above the park lodge.

destinations.name: Portillo
destinations.crowdNote: Hotel-capped numbers.
destinations.pitch: Legendary single-hotel resort on Laguna del Inca; steep chutes like the Super C.
destinations.avalanche: Andean: big storm cycles, wind; can close the pass road.
destinations.weather: Sunny high Andes; storms close the road for days.

children.name: Hotel Portillo
children.note: The yellow hotel and its lifts above Laguna del Inca.

children.name: Super C couloir
children.note: Classic hike-to couloir above the resort.

tours.name: Super C
tours.note: A long couloir reached by a hike from the top lift.

destinations.name: Santiago Three Valleys (Valle Nevado, La Parva, El Colorado)
destinations.crowdNote: Santiago weekends.
destinations.pitch: Big interconnected high-Andes terrain an hour from a capital city; heli-skiing on offer.
destinations.avalanche: High, dry Andes: strong winds build wind slabs; storm cycles are short and intense. Limited public forecasting.
destinations.weather: Mostly sunny; snow comes in a few big storms.

children.name: Valle Nevado
children.note: Biggest, Ikon.

children.name: La Parva
children.note: Locals' favourite, steeper.

children.name: El Colorado
children.note: Closest to Santiago.

children.name: Cajón del Maipo
children.note: Quieter touring in big valleys south-east of Santiago.

children.name: Cerro El Plomo
children.note: High ski-mountaineering peak above La Parva.

tours.name: Cerro El Plomo
tours.note: A high, serious objective with a long descent.

destinations.name: Las Leñas
destinations.crowdNote: Argentine winter holidays (July) get busy.
destinations.pitch: The Marte chair accesses vast steep chute terrain. Famous among freeriders, when Marte runs.
destinations.avalanche: Andean continental-ish: dry, wind-affected snowpack with wind slabs and some persistent layers; the Marte lift accesses big avalanche terrain.
destinations.weather: Wind often closes Marte; dry snow.

children.name: Las Leñas base
children.note: The resort village and lower lifts.

children.name: Marte
children.note: The famous lift to steep, big terrain.

destinations.name: Nevados de Chillán
destinations.pitch: Volcano resort with hot springs and Chile's longest run; big sidecountry.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime Andes: wet, heavy storms bring storm slabs and rain-on-snow; volcanic terrain with big open slopes.
destinations.weather: Stormier and snowier than central Chile.

children.name: Nevados de Chillán resort
children.note: Lifts on the volcano's flanks, with hot springs nearby.

children.name: Las Trancas
children.note: Village base down the road.

destinations.name: Bariloche (Cerro Catedral)
destinations.crowdNote: Very busy in July school holidays.
destinations.pitch: South America's largest resort over a Patagonian lake city; great sidecountry and Frey touring nearby.
destinations.avalanche: Patagonian maritime: wet storms and strong westerly winds bring storm and wind slabs; usually settles fast after storms.
destinations.weather: Variable, windy, mixed snow quality; lower base can be wet.

children.name: Cerro Catedral
children.note: Big ski area above Lake Nahuel Huapi.

children.name: Refugio López
children.note: Club Andino hut on Cerro López.

destinations.name: Bariloche Backcountry (Refugio Frey)
destinations.pitch: Granite spires and couloirs around Refugio Frey, accessed from Catedral.
destinations.avalanche: Patagonian maritime: wind and storm slabs dominate, with spring wet-snow cycles. No regular public forecast, so rely on local guides.
destinations.weather: Windy Patagonian weather windows.

children.name: Refugio Frey
children.note: Hut by a lake under granite spires.

children.name: Refugio San Martín (Jakob)
children.note: Hut in a deep valley to the west.

tours.name: Frey couloirs
tours.note: Steep lines between the granite spires.

destinations.name: Araucanía Volcanoes (Pucón)
destinations.pitch: Road trip skiing perfect volcanic cones (Villarrica, Llaima, Lonquimay) with hot springs and araucaria forests.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: spring corn cycles with wet slides in the afternoon, wind-scoured icy summits; crevasses on some glaciated cones.
destinations.weather: Storms then clear spells; spring is best.

children.name: Corralco (Lonquimay)
children.note: Ski resort on Lonquimay's flanks.

children.name: Villarrica
children.note: The classic active volcano above Pucón.

children.name: Lanín
children.note: Isolated cone across the border in Argentina.

children.name: Llaima
children.note: Big, active volcano in Conguillío park.

tours.name: Villarrica
tours.note: A climb past the smoking crater and a long corn descent.

tours.name: Lanín
tours.note: A big, isolated cone, usually over two days.

tours.name: Llaima
tours.note: Long descent with views of araucaria forests.

destinations.name: Ushuaia (Cerro Castor)
destinations.pitch: The southernmost resort on Earth; low-elevation but dependable cold snow; backcountry touring around.
destinations.avalanche: Sub-Antarctic maritime: frequent storms, strong winds and wind slabs; temperatures hover near freezing.
destinations.weather: Cold, windy, short days.

children.name: Cerro Castor
children.note: One of the southernmost ski areas in the world.

children.name: Valle de Tierra Mayor
children.note: Valley with touring and Nordic centres.

children.name: Martial glacier
children.note: Small glacier right above the city.

destinations.name: Antarctic Peninsula (sail & ski)
destinations.crowdNote: A handful of yachts per season.
destinations.pitch: Ski from sea to summit from expedition yachts among icebergs and penguins. The trip of a lifetime.
destinations.avalanche: Glaciated; crevasses, wind slab; no forecasting service.
destinations.weather: Fast-changing maritime weather; Drake crossing can be rough.

children.name: Port Lockroy
children.note: Former British base with a museum and post office.

children.name: Paradise Harbour
children.note: Sheltered bay ringed by glaciers and peaks.

children.name: Lemaire Channel
children.note: Narrow channel between steep walls of ice.

destinations.name: Chamonix Mont-Blanc
destinations.crowdNote: Grands Montets and Aiguille du Midi queues on powder days.
destinations.pitch: The world capital of alpinism and freeride: Vallée Blanche, Grands Montets, huge glaciated terrain. Gateway to the Haute Route.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps: mix of wind slabs and persistent layers; glacier hazards.
destinations.weather: Big Atlantic storms, foehn; the valley floor is low (1,035 m).

children.name: Grands Montets
children.note: Steep glacier freeride.

children.name: Aiguille du Midi (Vallée Blanche)
children.note: The 20 km glacier descent.

children.name: Brévent-Flégère
children.note: Sunny side, Mont Blanc views.

children.name: Le Tour-Balme
children.note: Mellow, good for beginners.

children.name: Refuge d'Argentière
children.note: Hut on the Argentière glacier, base for classic tours and the Haute Route start.

tours.name: Vallée Blanche
tours.note: About 20 km of glacier from the Aiguille du Midi to the Mer de Glace.

tours.name: Col du Passon
tours.note: A short classic tour from the Grands Montets lifts.

tours.name: Col du Chardonnet
tours.note: A bigger tour above the Argentière glacier, first stage of the Haute Route.

destinations.name: La Grave – La Meije
destinations.crowdNote: A single téléphérique and no pisting: rarely busy.
destinations.pitch: Just a cable car and 2,000 m of ungroomed, glaciated high-mountain freeride. Mythic. Pairs with Serre Chevalier.
destinations.avalanche: Southern French Alps: thinner snowpack, persistent layers possible.
destinations.weather: Sunny but winds close the lift; storms from both north and south.

children.name: La Grave–La Meije cable car
children.note: The two-section cable car from the village to about 3,200 m on the Girose glacier.
children.more: The whole freeride area hangs off this one lift. Wind closures are common.

children.name: Girose glacier
children.note: The glacier at the top, with a drag lift and access toward Les Deux Alpes.

children.name: Col du Lautaret
children.note: Classic ski-touring pass above the road, toward Combeynot and Galibier.
children.more: Moderate tours with easy access, popular with ski-touring groups.

children.name: Serre Chevalier
children.note: Big lift-served resort on the Briançon side: the backup on windy days.

children.name: Les Deux Alpes
children.note: Large resort over the glacier, reachable on skis from La Grave in good conditions.

tours.name: Vallons de la Meije
tours.note: The classic long descent from the top back to the village.

tours.name: Vallon de Chancel
tours.note: The other big classic, through glacial terrain under the Chancel refuge.

tours.name: Roc Noir de Combeynot
tours.note: A classic tour from the Col du Lautaret.

destinations.name: Les 3 Vallées (Courchevel, Méribel, Val Thorens)
destinations.crowdNote: February French school holidays are rammed.
destinations.pitch: The world's largest linked ski area (600 km of pistes); ski-in/ski-out at altitude.
destinations.avalanche: Northern French Alps: wind slabs and persistent layers in thin winters. In-bounds is controlled, but the off-piste is vast and not.
destinations.weather: High altitude (Val Thorens 2,300 m) keeps snow reliable.

children.name: Courchevel
children.note: Upscale, great groomers.

children.name: Méribel
children.note: Central, chalet village.

children.name: Val Thorens
children.note: Highest, snow-sure.

children.name: Les Menuires
children.note: Value option.

destinations.name: Val d'Isère & Tignes
destinations.pitch: High, snow-sure, and legendary off-piste (Espace Killy); glacier skiing at Tignes.
destinations.avalanche: Inner Alps-ish; persistent layers often present.
destinations.weather: Often catches 'retour d'Est' storms from Italy.

children.name: Val d'Isère
children.note: Village, Face de Bellevarde.

children.name: Tignes
children.note: High, glacier, purpose-built.

destinations.name: Paradiski (Les Arcs, La Plagne)
destinations.pitch: Huge linked area with purpose-built villages; very family-friendly; train-accessible.
destinations.avalanche: Northern French Alps: wind and storm slabs, persistent layers in thin winters. Off-piste is big and uncontrolled; the BRA forecast covers it.

children.name: Les Arcs
children.note: Varied, off-piste, funicular from Bourg.

children.name: La Plagne
children.note: Huge, family.

children.name: Peisey-Vallandry
children.note: Tree-lined sector between Les Arcs and the Vanoise Express.

destinations.name: Portes du Soleil (Avoriaz, Morzine, Champéry)
destinations.pitch: Cross-border circuit of 12 resorts; lower altitude, so check snow conditions.
destinations.avalanche: Pre-Alps, lower and wetter: storm slabs and wet-snow problems more than deep persistent layers. Off-piste is uncontrolled.
destinations.weather: Lower-altitude rain risk.

children.name: Avoriaz
children.note: Car-free, high, park.

children.name: Morzine
children.note: Real town, lower.

children.name: Champéry
children.note: Swiss side, the Wall.

children.name: Châtel
children.note: Quieter, value.

children.name: Les Gets
children.note: Wooded, family-friendly village linked to Morzine.

destinations.name: Alpe d'Huez
destinations.pitch: Sunny south-facing giant with the 16 km Sarenne black run.
destinations.avalanche: Western French Alps: wind slabs and persistent layers in thin winters; big off-piste (e.g. La Sarenne) is uncontrolled.
destinations.weather: Sunny.

children.name: Alpe d'Huez
children.note: The main village, at 1,860 m.

children.name: Vaujany
children.note: Quiet village linked by a big cable car.

children.name: Oz-en-Oisans
children.note: Wooded base, good on storm days.

children.name: Auris-en-Oisans
children.note: Small, sunny village on the area's southern side.

destinations.name: Verbier (4 Vallées)
destinations.crowdNote: Mont Fort and the Tortin lifts get crowded.
destinations.pitch: Freeride capital (Xtreme Verbier); off-piste right off the lifts, plus a huge linked piste network.
destinations.avalanche: Valais inner-Alpine: persistent weak layers common in thin winters.
destinations.weather: Drier inner-Alpine climate, sunny.

children.name: Verbier
children.note: The hub of the 4 Vallées.

children.name: Mont Fort
children.note: Top of the lifts at 3,330 m; the start of the big freeride and touring terrain.

children.name: Nendaz
children.note: Big family village on the 4 Vallées' other side.

children.name: Bruson
children.note: Quiet little area with good trees across the valley.

tours.name: Vallon d'Arbi
tours.note: Classic off-piste descent toward La Tzoumaz.

tours.name: Mont Gelé
tours.note: Steep, famous lines below an old lift.

tours.name: Rosablanche
tours.note: A classic tour from the top of the lifts, on the Haute Route.

destinations.name: Zermatt (+ Cervinia)
destinations.pitch: Car-free village under the Matterhorn, glacier skiing, and lunch in Italy. End of the Haute Route.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Valais): often thin, faceted snowpack with persistent weak layers; glacier hazards (crevasses) off-piste.
destinations.weather: Dry, sunny; one of the highest areas in the Alps.

children.name: Zermatt
children.note: Matterhorn village.

children.name: Breuil-Cervinia
children.note: Italian side, cheaper, sunny.

children.name: Breithorn
children.note: One of the easiest 4,000 m peaks, reached from the top of the glacier lifts.

tours.name: Breithorn (4,164 m)
tours.note: A short glacier climb from the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise.

tours.name: Stockhorn off-piste
tours.note: Big, high off-piste from the Gornergrat side.

destinations.name: Saas-Fee
destinations.pitch: Glacier village surrounded by thirteen 4,000 m peaks; snow-sure and quieter than Zermatt.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Valais) and glaciated: persistent weak layers in thin winters, crevasses off-piste; SLF forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Catches southern storms.

children.name: Saas-Fee
children.note: Car-free village under the Fee glacier.

children.name: Saas-Grund (Hohsaas)
children.note: Smaller, quieter area down the valley.

children.name: Allalinhorn
children.note: 4,027 m summit from the top of the Metro Alpin.

children.name: Britannia Hut
children.note: Hut for the Strahlhorn and other big glacier tours.

tours.name: Allalinhorn (4,027 m)
tours.note: A short climb from the Metro Alpin, one of the easiest 4,000ers.

tours.name: Strahlhorn (4,190 m)
tours.note: Classic big glacier tour from the Britannia Hut.

tours.name: Alphubel
tours.note: A big 4,000 m tour above the village.

destinations.name: Engelberg
destinations.crowdNote: Titlis tourists, but freeride lines quiet.
destinations.pitch: Titlis' 2,000 m freeride descents (Laub, Galtiberg); a Scandinavian freeride community; easy from Zurich.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps: big snowfalls bring storm and wind slabs; the famous Titlis off-piste is serious, glaciated avalanche terrain.
destinations.weather: Northern stau: frequent snow, also fog.

children.name: Titlis
children.note: Glacier summit with the big freeride lines.

children.name: Laub
children.note: Huge open face of about 1,000 m, visible from town.

children.name: Brunni
children.note: Small, sunny family area across the valley.

tours.name: Laub
tours.note: The famous 1,000 m open face.

tours.name: Galtiberg
tours.note: About 2,000 m of descent from the glacier to the valley.

tours.name: Steinberg
tours.note: Steep line through the glacier's seracs.

destinations.name: Andermatt
destinations.pitch: Gemsstock's steep freeride terrain at a snow crossroads catching storms from north and south.
destinations.avalanche: Central Alps, very snowy: frequent storm and wind slabs; the Gemsstock is steep, freeride-heavy avalanche terrain.
destinations.weather: Snowy: storms from both sides.

children.name: Gemsstock
children.note: Steep north-facing freeride mountain above town.

children.name: Oberalp Pass
children.note: Pass with lifts and classic ski tours.

children.name: Sedrun
children.note: Linked village on the Graubünden side.

children.name: Disentis
children.note: Linked area with good off-piste and a big monastery.

tours.name: Guspis valley
tours.note: Long, wild off-piste descent from the Gemsstock.

tours.name: Pazolastock
tours.note: A classic short tour from the Oberalp Pass.

destinations.name: St. Moritz & Engadin
destinations.pitch: Sunny high valley with Corviglia, Diavolezza glacier runs, and glamour.
destinations.avalanche: Inner-Alpine (Engadin): dry, cold and often thin, so weak faceted layers and persistent slabs are common. SLF forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Very sunny, cold, dry.

children.name: Corviglia (St. Moritz)
children.note: Sunny groomers.

children.name: Corvatsch
children.note: High, freeride Hahnensee run.

children.name: Diavolezza
children.note: Glacier descent under Piz Palü.

children.name: Bernina Pass
children.note: High pass with easy touring and lift access to Piz Lagalb nearby.

tours.name: Morteratsch glacier run

children.note: Outer-coast fishing village with steep peaks around.

children.name: Fjordgård
children.note: Village under dramatic ridges on the Ørnfjord side.

children.name: Husøy
children.note: Tiny island village linked by a causeway.

destinations.name: Narvikfjellet
destinations.pitch: Lift-accessed, steep fjord freeride above town; combine with Riksgränsen.
destinations.avalanche: Arctic coastal: wind slabs on open terrain above the trees; the off-piste from the top lift is steep and committing.

children.name: Narvikfjellet
children.note: Lift-served mountain above the town and fjord.

tours.name: Mørkhola
tours.note: The best-known steep couloir off the top.

destinations.name: Salten (Bodø & Sulitjelma)
destinations.crowdNote: A small local scene.
destinations.pitch: Coastal Arctic peaks behind Bodø, a big glacier on the Swedish border, and the world's strongest tidal current.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime snowpack. Norway's Varsom forecasts Salten.
destinations.weather: Mild and stormy on the coast; colder inland.

children.name: Børvasstindan
children.note: Jagged peaks just outside Bodø.

children.name: Sulitjelma
children.note: Old mining town below a big glacier.

destinations.name: Sunnmøre Alps
destinations.pitch: Fjord-to-summit classic (Hjørundfjord, Slogen) with historic hotels and boat access.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: storm and wind slabs, then spring wet-snow cycles on steep fjord-side slopes. varsom.no forecasts the region.
destinations.weather: Wet, variable; spring is reliable.

children.name: Slogen
children.note: The classic summit above Øye and the Hjørundfjord.

children.name: Saksa (Urke)
children.note: Big, steep descent above the village of Urke.

children.name: Kolåstinden
children.note: One of the highest peaks in the area.

children.name: Stranda
children.note: Lift-served freeride with fjord views.

tours.name: Slogen
tours.note: The classic: from the fjord to one of Norway's great views.

tours.name: Saksa
tours.note: Steep descent toward the fjord.

tours.name: Kolåstinden
tours.note: A big, popular summit.

destinations.name: Romsdal (Åndalsnes)
destinations.pitch: Big-wall valley with steep couloirs and fjord descents.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: storm and wind slabs; steep, big terrain above the fjord, with wet slides in spring.

children.name: Åndalsnes
children.note: Base town, with the Romsdal Gondola.

children.name: Isfjorden
children.note: Village north of Åndalsnes with classic tours.

children.name: Romsdalshorn
children.note: Iconic peak above the valley.

tours.name: Kirketaket
tours.note: A big, open classic with fjord views.

tours.name: Store Vengetind
tours.note: Steep, serious lines on one of Romsdal's big peaks.

destinations.name: Trollheimen & Innerdalen
destinations.crowdNote: Quiet, except Easter at the huts.
destinations.pitch: Classic Norwegian hut touring between three famous lodges, and one of Norway's most beautiful valleys.
destinations.avalanche: Transitional snowpack. Norway's Varsom forecasts Trollheimen.
destinations.weather: Coastal storms in the west, drier inland.

children.name: Gjevilvasshytta
children.note: One of the three classic huts.

children.name: Jøldalshytta
children.note: The northern hut of the triangle.

children.name: Trollheimshytta
children.note: The western hut of the triangle.

children.name: Innerdalen
children.note: Car-free valley under Innerdalstårnet.

tours.name: Trekanten (the triangle)
tours.note: Three days linking the classic huts.

tours.name: Snøtinden
tours.note: The highest peak in Trollheimen.

destinations.name: Svalbard
destinations.pitch: High-arctic ski expeditions by boat or snowmobile: glaciers, polar bears (armed guides required).
destinations.avalanche: Polar: thin, wind-affected snowpack with wind slabs and weak bases; glaciers, crevasses and polar bears add to the hazards.
destinations.weather: Cold, 24h daylight from late April.

permits.label: Travel rules and notification (Governor of Svalbard)

children.name: Longyearbyen
children.note: The main town and base for day tours.

children.name: Newtontoppen
children.note: Svalbard's highest peak, a remote expedition objective.

tours.name: Trollsteinen
tours.note: A classic day tour near Longyearbyen.

tours.name: Sarkofagen
tours.note: A short tour with views over the town and fjord.

destinations.name: Troll Peninsula
destinations.pitch: Peak-to-ocean heli and touring with long spring daylight and hot pools.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime sub-arctic: wind slabs and storm slabs; spring wet-snow cycles. The Icelandic Met Office forecasts north Iceland.
destinations.weather: Very changeable; down days likely.

children.name: Dalvík
children.note: Fishing town on the east side, with tours from town.

children.name: Klængshóll (Skíðadalur)
children.note: Heli-ski base in a side valley.

children.name: Siglufjörður
children.note: Town at the northern tip, steep peaks all around.

children.name: Hlíðarfjall (Akureyri)
children.note: Iceland's main lift-served ski area.

destinations.name: Westfjords
destinations.pitch: Remote, sailboat-based fjord touring.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: frequent storms, wind slabs and cornices; spring wet-snow cycles. Settlements here have a long avalanche history.
destinations.weather: Wild, windy.

children.name: Ísafjörður
children.note: Main town and base, with tours from town.

children.name: Tungudalur ski area
children.note: Small lift-served area for stormy days.

children.name: Hornstrandir
children.note: Uninhabited reserve, reached by boat.

destinations.name: Eastfjords (Seyðisfjörður)
destinations.crowdNote: Almost no visiting skiers.
destinations.pitch: Steep peaks over quiet fjord villages, two tiny ski areas, and a ferry from Denmark that docks at the bottom of the slopes.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime snowpack, with heavy storms. The Icelandic Met Office forecasts the Eastfjords.
destinations.weather: Stormy and snowy; calmer in spring.

children.name: Seyðisfjörður
children.note: Colourful fjord village and base.

children.name: Stafdalur ski area
children.note: Tiny ski area on the Fjarðarheiði pass.

children.name: Oddsskarð
children.note: Small ski area above Eskifjörður.

destinations.name: West Greenland (Maniitsoq & Sisimiut)
destinations.airport: Kangerlussuaq / Nuuk, then boat or heli
destinations.pitch: Expedition-yacht and heli skiing in empty fjords. Maniitsoq is called the 'Venice of the Arctic'.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecasting service: wind slabs dominate on open slopes, with spring wet-snow cycles. Go guided.
destinations.weather: Cold, stable spring highs; long days.

children.name: Maniitsoq
children.note: Town among the biggest, steepest coastal peaks.

children.name: Sisimiut
children.note: Larger town with more rounded, accessible terrain.

destinations.name: East Greenland (Tasiilaq)
destinations.pitch: The Ammassalik Alps: jagged peaks and sea ice; very remote.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecasting service: wind slabs and cornices on steep coastal peaks, glaciers in places. Go guided.
destinations.weather: Piteraq winds can be severe.

children.name: Tasiilaq
children.note: Inuit town and base for trips.

children.name: Kulusuk
children.note: Airport island and village.

destinations.name: Gudauri
destinations.pitch: Open, treeless freeride and cheap heli on the Georgian Military Highway; amazing food and wine.
destinations.avalanche: Caucasus: wind slabs on big, open, treeless slopes; persistent layers in thin winters. Freeride accidents are common, so hire a guide.
destinations.weather: Snowy, can be windy.

children.name: Gudauri resort
children.note: Lifts above 3,000 m over open slopes.

children.name: Kazbegi (Stepantsminda)
children.note: Touring base under Mount Kazbek.

tours.name: Mount Kazbek
tours.note: A serious spring ski ascent to about 5,050 m.

destinations.name: Svaneti (Mestia & Tetnuldi)
destinations.pitch: Medieval tower villages under 4,000-5,000 m Caucasus peaks; touring off small lifts.
destinations.avalanche: Caucasus: heavy snowfalls, wind slabs and persistent layers; big terrain with limited forecasting. Go guided.

children.name: Hatsvali
children.note: Small ski area just above Mestia.

children.name: Tetnuldi
children.note: Bigger, higher area with long open descents.

children.name: Ushguli
children.note: Tower villages under Shkhara.

destinations.name: Kaçkar Mountains Heli
destinations.pitch: Black Sea moisture onto the Pontic Alps: deep snow, lodge heli skiing.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime (Black Sea): heavy, wet snowfall with storm slabs; the heli operator runs its own avalanche program.
destinations.weather: Wet Black Sea storms.

children.name: Ayder
children.note: Mountain village with hot springs and touring above.

children.name: Kaçkar Dağı
children.note: The highest peak of the range.

destinations.name: Gulmarg
destinations.pitch: Himalayan gondola to almost 4,000 m with vast freeride for little money.
destinations.avalanche: Himalayan: big storms, persistent layers; limited forecasting.
destinations.weather: Western disturbances bring big dumps.
destinations.advisory: Some governments advise against travel to parts of Jammu & Kashmir. Check your government's current advice and your insurance.

children.name: Gulmarg (Kongdori)
children.note: Town and lower gondola stage, with tree skiing.

children.name: Apharwat ridge
children.note: Top of the gondola near 4,000 m, with big bowls.

tours.name: Back side to Drung
tours.note: Long descent off the back of Apharwat to a village.

destinations.name: Karakol & Tian Shan
destinations.pitch: Adventure: a small resort plus yurt-based touring and cat skiing in dry continental powder.
destinations.avalanche: Continental: cold, thin snowpack with depth hoar and a weak base; deep persistent slabs. Limited forecasting, so go with local guides.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry.

children.name: Karakol ski base
children.note: Small resort with forest runs above town.

children.name: Jyrgalan
children.note: Village with community-based touring.

children.name: Altyn-Arashan
children.note: Hot-spring valley and touring base.

destinations.name: Kamchatka Heli
destinations.pitch: Heli-skiing volcanoes that run down to the Pacific: one of the wildest heli destinations on Earth.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime volcanic: deep storm and wind slabs, big open volcano slopes; the heli operators manage avalanche risk.
destinations.weather: Pacific storms.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

children.name: Avachinsky
children.note: Volcano above the city, a popular ski ascent.

children.name: Vilyuchinsky
children.note: Coastal volcano with long heli runs.

children.name: Mutnovsky
children.note: Active volcano with a steaming crater.

tours.name: Avachinsky ascent
tours.note: A long day up the volcano above the city.

destinations.name: Niseko & Rusutsu
destinations.crowdNote: Very international and busy now: Hirafu lift lines, booked-out restaurants, Western prices.
destinations.pitch: JAPOW ground zero: relentless light snow off the Sea of Japan, gate-controlled off-piste, onsens.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime, often deep-snow cycles; Niseko local avalanche rules apply.
destinations.weather: Grey and snowing most days in Jan; cold, not much sun.

children.name: Niseko United (Grand Hirafu, Annupuri, Village, Hanazono)
children.note: Ikon. Busiest, most international.

children.name: Rusutsu
children.note: Epic. Uncrowded, great trees.

children.name: Mt Yōtei
children.note: The "Mount Fuji of Hokkaido", a classic crater tour.

tours.name: Mt Yōtei crater
tours.note: A long climb to the rim and steep lines into the crater.

tours.name: Annupuri summit
tours.note: Short hike from the top gates to open back-side bowls.
tours.area: Niseko United (Grand Hirafu, Annupuri, Village, Hanazono)

destinations.name: Kiroro & Sapporo resorts
destinations.crowdNote: Quieter than Niseko.
destinations.pitch: Kiroro is one of Hokkaido's deepest snow spots; Teine/Kokusai are day trips from Sapporo city.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime (Hokkaido west coast): frequent storm slabs from daily snowfall; tree wells and sluffs off-piste.
destinations.weather: Very snowy.

children.name: Kiroro
children.note: Very deep snow, resort hotels.

children.name: Sapporo Kokusai
children.note: Day trip, reliable.

children.name: Sapporo Teine
children.note: Olympic venue, sea views.

destinations.name: Furano & Central Hokkaido (Tomamu, Kamui)
destinations.crowdNote: Much more Japanese than Niseko.
destinations.pitch: Colder, drier inland Hokkaido powder; mix of resorts and a road trip to Asahidake.
destinations.avalanche: Inland Hokkaido: colder and drier, so facets and buried weak layers can form; storm slabs after big snowfalls.
destinations.weather: Coldest and driest snow in Japan.

children.name: Furano
children.note: Town-based, dry snow.

children.name: Hoshino Tomamu
children.note: Family resort complex.

children.name: Kamui Ski Links
children.note: Tiny, uncrowded tree skiing.

destinations.name: Asahidake
destinations.crowdNote: One ropeway: queues on powder mornings.
destinations.pitch: A single ropeway up Hokkaido's highest (steaming) volcano: ungroomed, ultra-dry powder in birch forest.
destinations.avalanche: Cold inland snowpack; volcano terrain; whiteouts.
destinations.weather: Cold and stormy; navigation is hard in whiteout.

children.name: Asahidake Ropeway
children.note: Single ropeway to about 1,600 m on the volcano.

children.name: Asahidake Onsen
children.note: Hot-spring village at the base.

destinations.name: Tokachi & Daisetsuzan Backcountry
destinations.pitch: Hut-based and road-access touring (Fukiage, Sandan-yama) in famously dry snow.
destinations.avalanche: Cold inland Hokkaido: persistent weak layers (facets, surface hoar) are more common than on the coast; storm slabs after big dumps.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry.

children.name: Fukiage Onsen
children.note: Trailhead with a free outdoor hot spring.

children.name: Sandan-yama
children.note: Classic tour with long tree runs.

children.name: Tokachidake
children.note: Active volcano with bigger, exposed slopes.

tours.name: Sandan-yama
tours.note: A classic tour from Fukiage.

destinations.name: Hakuba Valley
destinations.crowdNote: Westernised and busy at Happo-one; quieter at Cortina/Norikura.
destinations.pitch: Ten resorts under the Northern Alps, Olympic heritage, and serious backcountry in the Hakuba mountains.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime Honshu: very heavy snowfall loads slopes fast, so storm slabs and glide cracks; big alpine terrain above the resorts.
destinations.weather: Heavy snowfall but milder than Hokkaido: rain risk at the base later in the season.

children.name: Happo-one
children.note: Biggest, Olympic downhill.

children.name: Hakuba 47 / Goryu
children.note: Trees and park.

children.name: Hakuba Cortina
children.note: Deepest snow, open tree zones.

children.name: Iwatake
children.note: Views, mellow.

children.name: Tsugaike Kogen
children.note: Wide slopes and a gondola to the high plateau.

children.name: Hakuba Daisekkei
children.note: Huge snow gully, a classic spring tour.

tours.name: Hakuba Daisekkei
tours.note: One of Japan's biggest snow gullies, in spring.

destinations.name: Minakami & Tanigawa
destinations.crowdNote: Tokyo weekends; quiet midweek.
destinations.pitch: Deep Sea-of-Japan snow less than two hours from Tokyo, a ropeway into a notorious mountain, and onsen everywhere.
destinations.avalanche: Heavy maritime snow with storm slabs and glide cracks. The Japan Avalanche Network covers the area.
destinations.weather: Big storms from the Sea of Japan; the Tokyo side is sunny.

children.name: Tenjindaira (Tanigawadake)
children.note: Ropeway into steep backcountry on Tanigawadake.

children.name: Hodaigi
children.note: Wide, snowy slopes for storm days.

destinations.name: Myoko, Nozawa & Shiga Kogen
destinations.crowdNote: More Japanese, more traditional than Hakuba/Niseko.
destinations.pitch: Onsen villages (Nozawa), Japan's largest linked area (Shiga), and Myoko/Lotte Arai's deep snow.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime Honshu: very heavy loading brings storm slabs; tree wells and glide avalanches. Off-piste needs gate rules and care.
destinations.weather: Very snowy (Myoko), heavier snow than Hokkaido.

children.name: Myoko Kogen
children.note: Big snowfall, traditional.

children.name: Lotte Arai
children.note: Ikon. Huge snow, open off-piste.

children.name: Nozawa Onsen
children.note: Onsen village, fire festival.

children.name: Shiga Kogen
children.note: Japan's largest linked area, high and dry.

destinations.name: Hakkoda & Tohoku
destinations.pitch: A ropeway into backcountry known for 'snow monsters' (rime-coated trees); deep, cold and few foreigners. Pair with Zao.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: heavy snowfall, tree wells and navigation in flat light are bigger day-to-day issues than slabs; storm slabs after dumps.
destinations.weather: Cold, stormy, whiteouts.

children.name: Hakkoda Ropeway
children.note: Ropeway into the snow-monster backcountry.

children.name: Zao Onsen
children.note: Resort famous for snow monsters, with a hot-spring town.

children.name: Gassan
children.note: Volcano with spring skiing once the road clears.

children.name: Chōkai
children.note: Volcano with long spring descents toward the sea.

tours.name: Chōkai spring descent
tours.note: Around 2,000 m toward the Sea of Japan.

destinations.name: L+SNOW Shanghai
destinations.slope: Indoor: slopes for four levels, the longest 340 m at up to 26°
destinations.crowdNote: Chinese school holidays and summer weekends are very busy.
destinations.pitch: Certified by Guinness as the world's largest indoor ski resort when it opened in 2024: 90,000 m² of real snow, with ski-in, ski-out hotel rooms.
destinations.avalanche: None: it's indoors.
destinations.weather: Kept well below freezing inside; Shanghai summers are hot and humid outside.

destinations.name: Snowy Mountains (Thredbo, Perisher)
destinations.crowdNote: Sydney/Melbourne school holidays: very busy.
destinations.pitch: Australia's biggest areas; snowmaking-dependent, variable natural snow.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resorts, avalanche risk is low. In the backcountry: cornices and wind slabs on lee slopes, wet slides in spring.
destinations.weather: Marginal: rain and freeze-thaw are common.

children.name: Thredbo
children.note: Ikon. Most vertical.

children.name: Perisher
children.note: Epic. Largest area.

children.name: Charlotte Pass
children.note: Australia's highest resort village; reached by over-snow transport in winter.

destinations.name: Kosciuszko Main Range
destinations.pitch: Australia's alpine high point: day and overnight touring from Thredbo/Charlotte Pass; Western Faces.
destinations.avalanche: Cornices and wind slabs on lee slopes are the main problems; whiteouts and navigation are serious hazards too.
destinations.weather: Very changeable; whiteouts.

children.name: Charlotte Pass
children.note: Highest resort village; a classic starting point for the range.

children.name: Blue Lake
children.note: Glacial cirque lake with short, steep lines and cornices.

children.name: Mt Townsend
children.note: Second-highest peak in Australia, with steeper skiing than Kosciuszko.

children.name: Western Faces
children.note: Steep faces dropping over 1,000 m toward the Geehi valley.

children.name: Seaman's Hut
children.note: Historic stone emergency hut on the main track to Kosciuszko.

tours.name: Mount Kosciuszko
tours.note: Easy, scenic tour to the mainland's highest point from Thredbo or Charlotte Pass.

tours.name: The Sentinel
tours.note: A steep, prominent peak on the western side; a committing descent with a long climb out.

tours.name: Watsons Crags
tours.note: Steep chutes and ridges on the western faces; for experienced skiers in stable snow.

destinations.name: Victorian Alps (Falls Creek, Hotham, Buller)
destinations.pitch: Melbourne's playground; Hotham has the most expert terrain in Australia.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resorts, avalanche risk is low. In the backcountry: wind slabs and cornices on lee slopes, wet slides in spring.
destinations.weather: Marginal.

children.name: Falls Creek
children.note: Epic. Largest in Victoria.

children.name: Mt Hotham
children.note: Epic. Steepest in Australia.

children.name: Mt Buller
children.note: Ikon. Closest to Melbourne.

children.name: Bogong High Plains
children.note: Wide, gentle plains for ski touring and snow camping.

children.name: Mt Feathertop
children.note: Steep bowls and gullies, reached along the Razorback.

tours.name: Feathertop via the Razorback
tours.note: A long ridge tour from Mt Hotham to Victoria's most dramatic peak.

tours.name: Mount Bogong
tours.note: Victoria's highest peak (1,986 m), usually a multi-day trip on foot and skis via the Staircase Spur.

destinations.name: Queenstown & Wanaka
destinations.pitch: Four resorts (Remarkables, Coronet Peak, Cardrona, Treble Cone) and the adventure capital; heli everywhere.
destinations.avalanche: NZ maritime-transitional: storm and wind slabs; the snowpack usually stabilises quickly between storms.
destinations.weather: Big variability; nor'west winds.

children.name: The Remarkables
children.note: Ikon. Alpine bowls, park.

children.name: Coronet Peak
children.note: Ikon. Closest to town, night skiing.

children.name: Cardrona
children.note: Family and park.

children.name: Treble Cone
children.note: Steepest and biggest in NZ's south.

destinations.name: Mt Hutt
destinations.crowdNote: Road closures on windy days.
destinations.pitch: Big open bowl above the Canterbury Plains; Methven heli nearby.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime: storm and wind slabs after nor'west and southerly storms; big freeze-thaw swings make it icy.
destinations.weather: Wind-prone; often closed.

children.name: Methven
children.note: Ski town below the mountain and base for heli operators.

destinations.name: NZ Club Fields (Craigieburn, Broken River, Temple Basin)
destinations.pitch: Rope tows with nutcrackers, steep ungroomed terrain, club lodges. Unique and cheap.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime; uncontrolled terrain outside boundaries.
destinations.weather: Variable; NW storms.

children.name: Craigieburn Valley
children.note: Steep, ungroomed terrain on rope tows.

children.name: Broken River
children.note: Club field with great freeride and lodges on the hill.

children.name: Temple Basin
children.note: Walk-in field in Arthur's Pass with floodlit night skiing.

children.name: Mt Olympus
children.note: Remote and steep, with small lodges.

tours.name: Craigieburn–Broken River traverse
tours.note: A classic connection between the two club fields, over the ridge.

destinations.name: Southern Alps Heli & Tasman Glacier
destinations.pitch: Big-day heli from Wanaka/Methven/Queenstown, and ski-plane runs on the Tasman Glacier under Aoraki.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime alpine: storm and wind slabs; glacier hazards on the Tasman. Heli operators run professional avalanche programs.
destinations.weather: Weather days are common.

children.name: Tasman Glacier
children.note: Ski-plane and heli runs under Aoraki/Mount Cook.

children.name: Aoraki/Mount Cook village
children.note: Base for ski-plane and heli trips onto the Tasman.

tours.name: Tasman Glacier ski run
tours.note: Long, gentle glacier descent of about 10 km, through ice and crevasse fields.

destinations.name: Fiordland & the Milford Road
