destinations.pitch: Steep granite and glaciers off the Milford Road, from the NZAC's Homer Hut.
destinations.avalanche: Very wet maritime: storm slabs, big wet-snow cycles and huge avalanche paths onto the road.
destinations.weather: Very wet; storms straight off the Tasman Sea.

children.name: Homer Hut
children.note: NZ Alpine Club hut below the Homer Tunnel, the base for touring.

children.name: Gertrude Saddle
children.note: Steep pass with views down to Milford Sound.

tours.name: Gertrude Saddle
tours.note: Steep climb from the road end to a dramatic pass above Milford Sound.

destinations.name: Mt Ruapehu
destinations.pitch: Active volcano in the North Island with crater-lake ski touring; variable conditions.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime volcanic: rime ice and wind slabs; icy, wind-scoured terrain. Lahar hazard from the crater lake, too.
destinations.weather: Exposed, very variable.

children.name: Whakapapa
children.note: Big, varied terrain on the northern side.

children.name: Tūroa
children.note: High lift-served terrain and long runs on the south-western side.

children.name: Crater Lake
children.note: Summit crater lake, a classic tour from the top of the lifts.

tours.name: Crater Lake
tours.note: Climb from the top lifts to the summit plateau and ski back down.

destinations.name: Taranaki Maunga
destinations.pitch: Lone volcanic cone on the west coast: a tiny rope-tow club field and spring summit descents.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime volcanic: icy, wind-scoured upper slopes and slides into the gullies; falls on hard ice are the bigger killer.
destinations.weather: Close to the Tasman Sea, with fast-changing weather.

children.name: Manganui
children.note: Tiny club field with rope tows on the eastern slopes.

tours.name: Summit descent
tours.note: Spring ski descent from the summit cone, often icy on top and corn below.

destinations.name: Oukaïmeden
destinations.crowdNote: Marrakech day-trippers on weekends.
destinations.pitch: Ski Africa's highest lift-served slopes, an hour and a half from the Marrakech souks. Basic lifts, donkey 'lifts' and a big novelty factor.
destinations.avalanche: On piste, avalanche risk is low; snow cover is the bigger worry, as it is erratic year to year.
destinations.weather: Sunny; snow comes from a few Atlantic storms and can vanish fast.

destinations.name: Toubkal & High Atlas
destinations.pitch: Ski-tour North Africa's highest peak (4,167 m) from Berber villages and the Toubkal refuge, with mules carrying the gear.
destinations.avalanche: No forecasting service; wind slabs and icy spring snow.
destinations.weather: Unreliable snow years; sunny, cold nights.

children.name: Imlil
children.note: Berber village at the road end, where trips start.

children.name: Toubkal refuges
children.note: Huts at about 3,200 m, the base for the high peaks.

tours.name: Toubkal south cirque
tours.note: The usual ski route to North Africa's highest summit, about 1,000 m from the huts.

tours.name: Ouanoukrim
tours.note: Twin 4,000 m summits near the refuges, with steeper lines and couloirs.

destinations.name: Sierra Nevada (Granada)
destinations.crowdNote: Spanish weekends and holidays.
destinations.pitch: Europe's southernmost major resort: ski in the morning, Alhambra in the afternoon, and on clear days you can see Africa.
destinations.avalanche: On piste, avalanche risk is low. Off-piste: wind slabs and spring wet slides on steeper slopes.
destinations.weather: Very sunny; relies on snowmaking in dry years.

children.name: Pradollano
children.note: Resort village and base of the lifts.

children.name: Corral del Veleta
children.note: High cirque under Veleta with steeper off-piste.

tours.name: Mulhacén
tours.note: Mainland Spain's highest peak, a long tour along the ridge from the top of the resort road.

destinations.name: Crete: Lefka Ori
destinations.pitch: The White Mountains: ski-tour a lunar karst plateau with the Libyan Sea below, then eat in a taverna by the beach. Psiloritis is the other option.
destinations.avalanche: No forecasting service: wind slabs and spring wet-snow cycles on the high Lefka Ori. Go with local guides.
destinations.weather: Snow comes in short windows; very variable.

children.name: Kallergi refuge
children.note: Refuge above the Omalos plateau, the northern base.

children.name: Psiloritis
children.note: Crete's highest peak, in the centre of the island.

tours.name: Pachnes
tours.note: Highest peak of the White Mountains, with views to the Libyan Sea.

tours.name: Psiloritis from Nida
tours.note: Steady climb from the Nida plateau to the summit chapel.

destinations.name: Mount Etna
destinations.pitch: Ski-tour an active volcano above the Mediterranean, through steaming vents and black ash; two small lift areas too.
destinations.avalanche: Volcanic hazards; summit access is regulated.
destinations.weather: Windy summit; snow often gets ash-covered.

children.name: Etna Sud
children.note: South-side ski area near Rifugio Sapienza, with a cable car.

children.name: Etna Nord (Piano Provenzana)
children.note: Small north-side ski area.

tours.name: Toward the summit craters
tours.note: Climb past steaming vents and ski long, open slopes back down; access depends on volcanic activity.

tours.name: Valle del Bove
tours.note: A huge collapse valley on the east side; descents into it are a classic in good snow.

destinations.name: Afriski
destinations.crowdNote: South African school holidays.
destinations.pitch: One of only two ski resorts in Southern Africa, at 3,000 m in the 'Kingdom in the Sky'. Small and snowmaking-based, but unique.
destinations.avalanche: Inside the resort, avalanche risk is minimal: it is a small, gentle area.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry, sunny; little natural snow.

destinations.name: Ski Egypt
destinations.slope: Indoor: one main slope, about 210 m long
destinations.crowdNote: Busiest on Fridays, Saturdays and holidays.
destinations.pitch: Africa's first indoor ski slope, in a mall on the edge of Cairo: ski in the morning and see the Pyramids of Giza in the afternoon.
destinations.avalanche: None: it's indoors.
destinations.weather: Kept at about −2 °C inside, even when it's 40 °C outside.

destinations.name: Dizin & Shemshak
destinations.crowdNote: Tehran weekends (Thu-Fri).
destinations.pitch: High, dry Alborz powder an hour or two from Tehran: steep Shemshak, big open Dizin.
destinations.avalanche: Continental: wind slabs and persistent layers; limited public forecasting. Off-piste at Dizin and Shemshak is big terrain.
destinations.weather: Dry snow, sunny.

children.name: Dizin
children.note: Biggest and highest, open bowls.

children.name: Shemshak
children.note: Steep, mogul-heavy.

children.name: Tochal
children.note: Reached by a long gondola from Tehran.

destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against travel to Iran, and dual nationals face particular risks. Check your government's current advice before planning.

destinations.name: Mount Damavand
destinations.pitch: Ski a 5,610 m volcano, the highest in Asia, from the Bargah-e Sevom hut: a big-altitude spring descent.
destinations.avalanche: High-altitude; fumaroles; altitude sickness is the main risk.
destinations.weather: Spring stability; high winds at the summit.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against travel to Iran, and dual nationals face particular risks. Check your government's current advice before planning.

children.name: Polour
children.note: Village at the foot and climbers' base.

children.name: Bargah-e Sevom hut
children.note: High hut at about 4,150 m.

tours.name: South route to the summit
tours.note: 8 to 12 hours up; a huge descent back.

destinations.name: Mzaar & The Cedars
destinations.crowdNote: Beirut weekends.
destinations.pitch: Ski in the morning, Mediterranean beach in the afternoon. The Cedars sits above an ancient cedar grove.
destinations.avalanche: On piste, avalanche risk is low. Off-piste: wind slabs and wet-snow cycles on open slopes.
destinations.weather: Wet Mediterranean storms; variable.

children.name: Mzaar Kfardebian
children.note: Largest resort, 1h from Beirut.

children.name: The Cedars
children.note: Highest, by the Cedars of God grove.

destinations.advisory: Advice for Lebanon changes quickly, and some areas are no-go. Check your government's current advice before planning.

destinations.name: Ski Dubai
destinations.slope: Indoor: five runs, the longest about 400 m with a drop of about 60 m
destinations.crowdNote: Busiest at weekends and in school holidays; weekday mornings are quietest.
destinations.pitch: Real snow inside a Dubai shopping mall, with a chairlift, a 400 m run and a colony of penguins. Pure novelty, and great fun as a stopover.
destinations.avalanche: None: it's indoors.
destinations.weather: Kept below freezing inside, whatever the desert heat outside.

destinations.name: Mauna Kea
destinations.pitch: Ski a 4,200 m tropical volcano by 4x4 shuttle, then surf the same day. Only after rare winter storms, so it's an opportunistic trip.
destinations.avalanche: Rocky and icy; high altitude; summit is sacred, so respect closures.
destinations.weather: Snow is rare and melts fast.

destinations.name: Wolf Creek
destinations.crowdNote: Remote: weekend Texans and New Mexicans, otherwise quiet.
destinations.pitch: The most snow in Colorado, an independent family-owned hill, and a cheap ticket. Pairs with Taos or Silverton.
destinations.avalanche: San Juan continental: one of the weakest snowpacks in the US, with deep persistent slabs. Heavy snowfall helps in-bounds.
destinations.weather: Big San Juan storms.

children.name: Wolf Creek Ski Area
children.note: Colorado's snowiest resort, family-owned, with hike-to steeps.

children.name: Wolf Creek Pass
children.note: Backcountry and Nordic terrain on the Divide, next to the ski area.

destinations.name: Kachina Peaks (Flagstaff)
destinations.crowdNote: Busy after storms near Snowbowl; empty further in.
destinations.pitch: Arizona's highest mountain: an old volcano above the desert, with its own avalanche center and bowls that fill in big storm years.
destinations.avalanche: Thin, variable Southwest snowpack with weak layers. The Kachina Peaks Avalanche Center forecasts the San Francisco Peaks.
destinations.weather: Boom-and-bust: big Pacific storms, then long dry, sunny spells.

children.name: Arizona Snowbowl
children.note: The ski area on the western side; the main access to the Peaks.

children.name: Humphreys Peak
children.note: Arizona's highest summit, with bowls and avalanche paths below.

children.name: Inner Basin · Lockett Meadow
children.note: The collapsed caldera, reached by a long approach from the east.

tours.name: Humphreys Peak
tours.note: A big-year ski descent from Arizona's highest point.

tours.name: Inner Basin
tours.note: A long, quiet tour into the heart of the old volcano.

destinations.name: Winter Park & Mary Jane
destinations.crowdNote: Denver weekends; the ski train helps.
destinations.pitch: Denver's local giant: Mary Jane's famous bumps, Winter Park's cruisers, and a direct ski train from Union Station.
destinations.avalanche: Colorado continental: faceted base layers and persistent slabs off-piste; in-bounds terrain is controlled.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry.

destinations.name: Ogden Valley (Snowbasin & Powder Mountain)
destinations.crowdNote: Far quieter than the Cottonwoods.
destinations.pitch: Uncrowded Utah: Snowbasin's Olympic terrain and lodges, and Powder Mountain's cap on daily ticket sales.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain: early-season facets can leave a buried persistent weak layer; the Utah Avalanche Center forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Utah powder.

children.name: Snowbasin
children.note: Olympic downhill, plush lodges.

children.name: Powder Mountain
children.note: Huge acreage, capped skier numbers.

children.name: Ben Lomond Peak
children.note: Prominent peak at the north end of the Ogden Valley, with backcountry terrain.

destinations.name: Whitefish & Flathead
destinations.crowdNote: Busy weekends and holidays; quiet otherwise.
destinations.pitch: A friendly Montana mountain with snow ghosts, views of Glacier National Park, and a train that stops in town.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain snowpack. The Flathead Avalanche Center forecasts the Whitefish, Swan and Flathead ranges and Glacier National Park.
destinations.weather: Often foggy and rimed at the top; cold and snowy.

children.name: Whitefish Mountain Resort
children.note: Big Mountain, with snow ghosts and park views.

children.name: Marias Pass
children.note: Roadside touring on the Continental Divide at the edge of Glacier NP.

children.name: Essex · Izaak Walton Inn
children.note: Historic railway hotel with Nordic trails and nearby touring.

destinations.name: McCall & Payette (Brundage, Tamarack)
destinations.crowdNote: Boise on weekends, quiet midweek.
destinations.pitch: A lakeside Idaho town with two low-key resorts, cat skiing and light, deep snow.
destinations.avalanche: Intermountain snowpack. The Payette Avalanche Center forecasts the area.
destinations.weather: Steady storms and cold snow; inversions bring fog in the valley.

children.name: Brundage Mountain
children.note: Snowy local resort north of McCall, with cat skiing.

children.name: Tamarack Resort
children.note: Newer resort above Lake Cascade.

destinations.name: La Sal Mountains (Moab)
destinations.crowdNote: A handful of locals on a busy day.
destinations.airport: Grand Junction (GJT) 2 h / Moab (CNY) / Salt Lake City (SLC) 4 h
destinations.pitch: Desert peaks above Moab, with snowy bowls looking out over the red-rock canyons of Arches and Canyonlands.
destinations.avalanche: Thin continental snowpack, often weak. The Utah Avalanche Center runs a dedicated Moab forecast.
destinations.weather: Dry and cold, with storms from the south and west.

children.name: Geyser Pass trailhead
children.note: Plowed winter trailhead, the main access to the backcountry.

children.name: Gold Basin
children.note: The heart of the La Sal backcountry, below Tuk and Mellenthin.

tours.name: Mount Tukuhnikivatz
tours.note: The local classic, with steep lines off the summit.

tours.name: Gold Basin tree runs
tours.note: Mellower terrain for unstable days.

destinations.name: Jotunheimen huts
destinations.crowdNote: Busy over Easter.
destinations.airport: Oslo, then 5h drive or train to Otta
destinations.pitch: Norway's highest mountains (Galdhøpiggen, Glittertind) on a DNT hut network: classic Easter and spring touring, glacier day trips from Juvasshytta and Spiterstulen.
destinations.avalanche: Continental-ish spring snowpack; varsom.no forecasts.
destinations.weather: Cold, clear spring highs; long days.

children.name: Juvasshytta
children.note: High lodge, the usual start for Galdhøpiggen.

children.name: Spiterstulen
children.note: Lodge in the Visdalen valley, base for Glittertind.

children.name: Galdhøpiggen
children.note: Highest peak in Northern Europe.

tours.name: Galdhøpiggen (2,469 m)
tours.note: From Juvasshytta across the glacier.

tours.name: Glittertind
tours.note: A long tour from Spiterstulen.

destinations.name: Bernese Oberland Haute Route
destinations.airport: Zurich / Bern by train to Jungfraujoch
destinations.pitch: Ride the train to the Jungfraujoch and tour the Aletsch glacier world between big huts (Konkordia, Finsteraarhorn): Switzerland's grandest hut tour.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Alps, glaciated high alpine: wind slabs and spring wet-snow cycles; crevasses on the glacier passes.
destinations.weather: High altitude weather windows.

children.name: Jungfraujoch
children.note: The start: a train to 3,454 m.

children.name: Konkordia Hut
children.note: Cliff-top hut above the Konkordiaplatz.

children.name: Finsteraarhorn Hut
children.note: Base for the Finsteraarhorn.

children.name: Hollandia Hut
children.note: Hut on the Lötschenlücke, above the Lötschental exit.

tours.name: Finsteraarhorn (4,274 m)
tours.note: Highest peak in the Bernese Alps; a ski depot then a ridge.

tours.name: Lötschenlücke to the Lötschental
tours.note: The classic exit, a long descent.

destinations.name: Écrins huts
destinations.pitch: Big, wild glaciated massif around the Barre des Écrins, with the Dôme des Écrins as a classic 4,000 m ski summit. Wilder and quieter than Chamonix.
destinations.avalanche: Southern Alps: thinner snowpack, persistent layers.
destinations.weather: Sunny southern Alps.

children.name: Refuge des Écrins
children.note: High hut on the Glacier Blanc, base for the Dôme.

children.name: Refuge du Glacier Blanc
children.note: Lower hut on the way up the glacier.

children.name: Névache valley
children.note: Gentle touring and cosy refuges near Briançon.

tours.name: Dôme de Neige des Écrins (4,015 m)
tours.note: Classic ski 4,000er from the Écrins hut.

tours.name: Roche Faurio
tours.note: A popular summit across the glacier from the hut.

destinations.name: Vanoise Haute Route
destinations.pitch: Hut-to-hut glacier traverse through France's first national park, between Pralognan and Val d'Isère.
destinations.avalanche: Inner Alps: persistent weak layers in thin winters, wind slabs, and spring wet-snow cycles; glaciers on parts of the route.

children.name: Pralognan-la-Vanoise
children.note: Usual starting village, below the Grande Casse.

children.name: Refuge de l'Arpont
children.note: Hut below the Vanoise glaciers.

children.name: Bonneval-sur-Arc
children.note: Beautiful stone village at the eastern end.

tours.name: Dôme de Chasseforêt
tours.note: Easy glacier summit with big views.

tours.name: Dôme de l'Arpont
tours.note: A classic summit above the Arpont hut.

destinations.name: Stubai Alps huts
destinations.pitch: Austria's classic hut-touring week: dense hut network (Franz-Senn, Amberger), lots of 3,000 m summits, 40 minutes from Innsbruck.
destinations.avalanche: Northern Tyrol, glaciated: wind slabs and persistent layers; crevasses above the huts. avalanche.report forecasts daily.

children.name: Franz-Senn-Hütte
children.note: Classic touring hut with peaks all around.

children.name: Amberger Hütte
children.note: Hut for the Schrankogel and nearby peaks.

children.name: Stubai Glacier
children.note: Austria's largest glacier ski area.

tours.name: Ruderhofspitze
tours.note: A big summit from the Franz-Senn-Hütte.

tours.name: Schrankogel (3,497 m)
tours.note: A big objective from the Amberger Hütte.

destinations.name: Ortler & Cevedale
destinations.pitch: High glaciated touring from the Casati and Branca huts: Cevedale and Palon de la Mare are classic ski summits.
destinations.avalanche: Southern/inner Alps, glaciated: wind slabs and persistent layers in thin winters; crevasses and seracs on the big peaks.

children.name: Rifugio Branca
children.note: Hut in the Forni valley, below the glaciers.

children.name: Rifugio Casati
children.note: High hut on the pass below the Cevedale.

children.name: Santa Caterina Valfurva
children.note: Small resort and the main base.

children.name: Solda (Sulden)
children.note: Village under the Ortler, with lifts.

tours.name: Cevedale (3,769 m)
tours.note: A big, rounded glacier summit.

tours.name: Palon de la Mare
tours.note: One of the best ski 3,000ers in the Alps.

destinations.name: Pyrenees Haute Route
destinations.pitch: Hut-to-hut across the central Pyrenees (Gavarnie to Aneto) with Spanish food and fewer people than the Alps.
destinations.avalanche: Pyrenees: wind slabs and wet-snow cycles; the snowpack can be thin on the Spanish side. Météo-France and AEMET forecast.
destinations.weather: Atlantic storms vs Mediterranean sun.

children.name: Gavarnie
children.note: The start, under the famous cirque.

children.name: Refugio de Góriz
children.note: Hut below Monte Perdido.

children.name: Refugio de la Renclusa
children.note: Hut for the Aneto, above Benasque.

tours.name: Aneto (3,404 m)
tours.note: The highest peak in the Pyrenees; short ridge on foot.

tours.name: Monte Perdido
tours.note: Big limestone peak above Ordesa.

tours.name: Vignemale
tours.note: Big glacier peak on the border.

destinations.name: Wapta Icefield Traverse
destinations.pitch: The Rockies' classic hut-to-hut glacier traverse (Bow, Peyto, Balfour, Scott Duncan huts) off the Icefields Parkway.
destinations.avalanche: Rockies continental, glaciated: weak, faceted base layers, wind slabs on the icefield edges, and crevasses.
destinations.weather: Cold; spring stability.

children.name: Bow Hut
children.note: The usual start, above Bow Lake. A good base on its own.

children.name: Peyto Hut
children.note: Northern hut on the Wapta, near Mount Baker and the Peyto Glacier.

children.name: Balfour Hut
children.note: Below Mount Balfour, before the high col.

children.name: Scott Duncan Hut
children.note: The last hut, perched above the descent to Sherbrooke Lake.

tours.name: Mount Gordon
tours.note: A popular, straightforward summit from the Bow Hut.

tours.name: Mount Olive
tours.note: A classic peak near the Bow Hut.

tours.name: The full Wapta Traverse
tours.note: Bow to Scott Duncan over four to six days.

destinations.name: Pine Pass (North Rockies)
destinations.crowdNote: A local scene from Prince George and the Peace region.
destinations.pitch: Deep, reliable snow at the north end of the Rockies, with roadside touring and a snowy local ski hill.
destinations.avalanche: Transitional snowpack. Avalanche Canada's North Rockies forecast covers the area.
destinations.weather: Snowy and cold, with frequent storms.

children.name: Powder King
children.note: Small, snowy ski area near the pass.

children.name: Pine Pass
children.note: Roadside touring on Highway 97.

destinations.name: Kananaskis Country
destinations.crowdNote: Busy weekend trailheads from Calgary.
destinations.pitch: Calgary's backyard: classic Rockies day tours off the Smith-Dorrien road, plus an Olympic ski area.
destinations.avalanche: Thin, cold Rockies snowpack with deep persistent layers. Kananaskis Country Public Safety forecasts on avalanche.ca.
destinations.weather: Cold and dry, with chinook winds that can warm things up fast.

children.name: Nakiska
children.note: Olympic ski area from 1988.

children.name: Burstall Pass
children.note: Classic long tour to a high pass on the Banff boundary.

children.name: Chester Lake
children.note: Popular tour with bowls above a frozen lake.

tours.name: Burstall Pass
tours.note: A long, gentle approach to big views.

tours.name: Chester Lake
tours.note: Popular tour with bowls above the lake.

tours.name: Rummel Lake
tours.note: A short, low-angle tour for unstable days.

destinations.name: Jasper (Marmot Basin)
destinations.crowdNote: One of the quietest big resorts in the Rockies.
destinations.pitch: A quiet resort in a huge national park, with glacier touring on the Icefields Parkway and lots of wildlife.
destinations.avalanche: Rockies continental snowpack, often with persistent weak layers. Parks Canada forecasts Jasper on avalanche.ca.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry and often clear; deep cold snaps.

children.name: Marmot Basin
children.note: Jasper's ski area, quiet and varied.

children.name: Bald Hills (Maligne Lake)
children.note: Gentle, open touring above Maligne Lake.

children.name: Columbia Icefield
children.note: Glacier skiing and ski mountaineering on the Icefields Parkway.

tours.name: Bald Hills
tours.note: Open, rolling touring with big views.

tours.name: Mount Athabasca
tours.note: Spring glacier ski mountaineering.

destinations.name: Sierra High Route
destinations.pitch: The 'Sierra High Route': a committing 6-7 day spring traverse across the High Sierra near Mt Whitney, camping or tenting rather than huts.
destinations.avalanche: Spring Sierra: corn cycles with afternoon wet slides; big storm cycles can still bring storm slabs.
destinations.weather: Stable spring sun.

children.name: Symmes Creek trailhead
children.note: The classic start, near Independence, climbing to Shepherd Pass.

children.name: Pear Lake Ski Hut
children.note: Bookable winter hut in Sequoia National Park, near the end of the route.

tours.name: Sierra High Route, east to west
tours.note: The full traverse from Symmes Creek to Wolverton.

tours.name: Pear Lake Ski Hut
tours.note: A shorter trip on its own: a few days of touring from the hut.

destinations.name: Tateyama Kurobe
destinations.pitch: Spring-only: the Alpine Route opens in mid-April to giant snow walls, giving access to huge Northern Alps couloirs from mountain huts at Murodo.
destinations.avalanche: Spring snowpack: wet-snow avalanches and cornice collapses as it warms; huge snow depths from winter.
destinations.weather: Clear spring weather; deep snowpack.

children.name: Murodo
children.note: High bus stop and huts on the Alpine Route.

children.name: Tsurugi
children.note: Steep peak with serious couloirs.

tours.name: Oyama (Tateyama)
tours.note: The main summit, from Murodo.

destinations.name: High Tatras
destinations.pitch: Compact granite range with steep couloirs and mountain huts (chaty), cheap and accessible from Kraków or Poprad.
destinations.avalanche: Continental; strict national park rules on routes.
destinations.weather: Cold, variable.

children.name: Kasprowy Wierch
children.note: Cable car above Zakopane and classic freeride valleys.

children.name: Tatranská Lomnica
children.note: Slovak resort with the Lomnický štít cable car.

children.name: Štrbské Pleso
children.note: Small resort by a lake on the Slovak side.

tours.name: Gąsienicowa valley
tours.note: Classic freeride below Kasprowy Wierch.

destinations.name: Krkonoše (Giant Mountains)
destinations.crowdNote: Very popular with Czech and Polish skiers.
destinations.pitch: Low, windswept Central European mountains with real avalanche cirques, cheap resorts and a mountain-rescue forecast.
destinations.avalanche: Wind-loaded cirques can produce real avalanches. The Czech Mountain Rescue Service forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Windy and often foggy; rime-covered trees.

children.name: Špindlerův Mlýn
children.note: The main resort, with the steepest runs in Czechia.

children.name: Pec pod Sněžkou
children.note: Resort below Sněžka.

children.name: Obří důl
children.note: Glacial cirque under Sněžka, avalanche terrain.

destinations.name: Jasná (Low Tatras)
destinations.crowdNote: Busy weekends and Slovak holidays.
destinations.airport: Poprad (TAT) 1 h / Kraków 3 h / Bratislava 4 h
destinations.pitch: Slovakia's biggest resort, on both sides of a mountain, with marked freeride zones and good value.
destinations.avalanche: Central European continental snowpack; the Slovak avalanche service (laviny.sk) forecasts daily.
destinations.weather: Cold, with wind on the Chopok summit.

children.name: Jasná north side
children.note: The main side, with steeper runs and freeride zones.

children.name: Chopok south side
children.note: Sunnier, gentler side of the mountain.

destinations.name: Sochi: Krasnaya Polyana
destinations.crowdNote: Busy Russian holidays (early Jan).
destinations.pitch: The 2014 Olympic cluster: big modern lift systems 1 hour from the Black Sea, with lots of tree and sidecountry terrain.
destinations.avalanche: Maritime Caucasus: heavy snowfall brings storm slabs; big, steep terrain off-piste at Rosa Khutor.
destinations.weather: Black Sea moisture brings big, wet dumps; the lower slopes can see rain.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

children.name: Rosa Khutor
children.note: Largest, Olympic alpine venue.

children.name: Gazprom Laura & Polyana
children.note: Modern, family.

children.name: Krasnaya Polyana resort
children.note: Steepest, freeride.

destinations.name: Elbrus Region (Cheget & Elbrus)
destinations.pitch: Old-school Soviet lifts on Cheget and the Elbrus cable car give huge, cheap freeride under Europe's highest peak.
destinations.avalanche: Caucasus continental; big avalanche paths, limited control.
destinations.weather: High and cold; storms close lifts.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

children.name: Cheget
children.note: Old lifts, steep and varied freeride.

children.name: Elbrus (Azau)
children.note: Modern cable car to about 3,850 m.

destinations.name: Mount Elbrus Summit Descent
destinations.crowdNote: Busy with climbers in summer, quiet in spring.
destinations.pitch: Ski off the highest summit in Europe (5,642 m): a spring acclimatisation expedition with one of the world's great volcano descents.
destinations.avalanche: High altitude, crevasses, ice; whiteouts are the classic killer.
destinations.weather: Severe summit winds and cold; tight weather windows.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

children.name: Garabashi (barrel huts)
children.note: Barrel huts at the top of the lifts, base for the climb.

tours.name: South route to the summit
tours.note: About 1,800 m from the huts; altitude is the challenge.

destinations.name: Dombai & Arkhyz
destinations.pitch: Dramatic Caucasus peaks (Dombai) and a fast-growing modern resort (Arkhyz, voted Russia's best). Cheap, with big off-piste.
destinations.avalanche: Caucasus: heavy snowfall with storm and wind slabs; steep terrain and limited forecasting. Go with local guides.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

children.name: Dombai
children.note: Classic, steep, spectacular.

children.name: Arkhyz Romantik
children.note: New, modern, family.

destinations.name: Khibiny (Kirovsk)
destinations.pitch: Arctic freeride and touring above the Kola Peninsula: open bowls, a long spring season, and midnight sun in May.
destinations.avalanche: Arctic; well-known avalanche centre in Kirovsk; wind slabs.
destinations.weather: Polar night in Dec-Jan; spring is best.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

children.name: Bolshoy Vudyavr
children.note: Main ski area above Kirovsk.

destinations.name: Sheregesh
destinations.crowdNote: Famous party weekends.
destinations.pitch: Siberia's powder capital: deep, very cold, dry snow in birch and fir forests, with a famous spring party scene.
destinations.avalanche: Mostly tree skiing; cold continental snowpack.
destinations.weather: Very cold (−25 °C is normal); deep snow.
destinations.advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

destinations.name: Almaty: Shymbulak backcountry
destinations.crowdNote: City weekends at Shymbulak.
destinations.pitch: A gondola from a big, cheap city straight into the Tian Shan: lift-served freeride above Shymbulak and a 4,000 m wall rising behind Almaty.
destinations.avalanche: Continental Tian Shan: significant avalanche risk and limited rescue.
destinations.weather: Sunny, cold, dry snow.

children.name: Shymbulak
children.note: The main resort, gondola from the city.

children.name: Ak Bulak
children.note: Small resort, lift-assisted touring.

children.name: Talgar pass
children.note: Top of Shymbulak at about 3,200 m.

destinations.name: Trans-Ili Alatau huts & yurts
destinations.pitch: Multi-day touring from yurts, mountain huts and an old Soviet observatory: Bogdanovich Glacier above Shymbulak, the Turgen Gorge, and the Ketmen ridge to the east.
destinations.avalanche: Continental; deep weak layers; very limited rescue.
destinations.weather: Dry, cold, sunny between storms.

children.name: Tuyuksu glacier
children.note: High, well-studied glacier above Shymbulak.

children.name: Big Almaty Lake
children.note: Turquoise lake with an old observatory nearby.

children.name: Turgen gorge
children.note: Wilder, quieter touring further east.

destinations.name: Fanes-Senes-Braies (Dolomites)
destinations.pitch: Quiet Dolomites touring through a nature park of limestone plateaus, with excellent rifugi (Fanes, Lavarella) between Cortina and Alta Badia.
destinations.avalanche: Southern Alps: often thin, faceted snowpack with persistent weak layers; wind slabs in the high cirques.
destinations.weather: Sunny; depends on southern storms.

children.name: Pederü
children.note: Road-end hut and the usual start.

children.name: Rifugio Fanes & Lavarella
children.note: Two rifugi on the Fanes plateau.

children.name: Rifugio Sennes
children.note: Hut on the wide Sennes plateau.

tours.name: Col Becchei
tours.note: A summit with big views over the plateau.

tours.name: Piz Lavarella
tours.note: A steeper, rockier summit above the hut.

destinations.name: Baffin Island (Clyde River & Sam Ford Fjord)
destinations.crowdNote: A handful of teams each spring.
destinations.pitch: Big-wall fjords and 1,000 m couloirs straight off the sea ice, from tent camps reached by Inuit-run snowmobile.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; cold, dry high-arctic snowpack. Self-reliance and polar-bear protection required.
destinations.weather: Very cold in April, milder in May; 24-hour daylight by mid-May.

children.name: Clyde River
children.note: Inuit community and starting point.

children.name: Sam Ford Fjord
children.note: Fjord of granite walls and long couloirs.

children.name: Ruth Gorge (Sheldon Amphitheater)
children.note: Glacier touring under huge granite walls, with a hut on a nunatak.

children.name: Kahiltna base camp
children.note: Landing strip and base camp for the West Buttress.

destinations.name: Denali & Ruth Gorge
destinations.crowdNote: Busy West Buttress camps in late May; Ruth Gorge is quiet.
destinations.pitch: North America's highest peak, guided on skis since 2022, or glacier ski touring under the granite walls of Ruth Gorge.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast; glacier travel and crevasse rescue skills essential.
destinations.weather: Extreme cold and wind high up; storms can pin teams for days.

tours.name: Ruth Gorge glacier touring
tours.note: Days of touring from a camp or the Mountain House.

tours.name: West Buttress
tours.note: The standard Denali route; skiing on the lower and middle mountain.

destinations.name: Mera Peak
destinations.crowdNote: A popular trekking peak; skiers are few.
destinations.pitch: The Himalaya's classic ski objective: a gentle glacier from 6,476 m with Everest, Lhotse and Makalu on the horizon.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; guides manage glacier and altitude risk.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry and stable in the pre- and post-monsoon windows.

children.name: Khare
children.note: Last settlement below the glacier.

children.name: Mera high camp
children.note: Camp on the glacier below the summit.

tours.name: Mera Peak summit descent
tours.note: A long, gentle glacier descent from near 6,476 m.

destinations.name: Annapurna Sanctuary
destinations.crowdNote: Trekkers on the trail; nobody on skis.
destinations.pitch: Ski touring inside a ring of 7,000 and 8,000 m peaks from the lodges at Annapurna Base Camp.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; the sanctuary approach is notorious for avalanche paths.
destinations.weather: Cold clear mornings, afternoon cloud; late-winter snow.

children.name: Annapurna Base Camp
children.note: Lodges at about 4,130 m inside the sanctuary.

destinations.name: Muztagh Ata
destinations.crowdNote: A few commercial teams each July.
destinations.pitch: The 7,546 m 'father of ice mountains': the classic first 7,000 m peak to ski, with a broad glacier from near the summit.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; high-altitude glacier travel.
destinations.weather: Thin air, strong sun, sudden storms; summer is the stable window.
destinations.advisory: Xinjiang has pervasive police checkpoints and surveillance; border areas (including Hemu/Kanas and the Pamir) need extra permits, and some travellers also weigh the region's human-rights situation. Check your government's travel advice.

children.name: Karakul Lake
children.note: Lake at the foot of the mountain.

children.name: Muztagh Ata base camp
children.note: West-side base camp for the standard route.

tours.name: West route
tours.note: Wide, open slopes through high camps to the summit plateau.

children.name: Cayambe
children.note: Glaciated volcano almost on the equator.

children.name: Cotopaxi
children.note: One of the highest active volcanoes in the world.

children.name: Chimborazo
children.note: Summit farthest from the Earth's centre.

destinations.name: Ecuador's Volcanoes (Cayambe, Cotopaxi, Chimborazo)
destinations.crowdNote: Climbers on the standard routes; few skiers.
destinations.pitch: Ski glaciated volcanoes on the equator, ending on Chimborazo: the point on Earth farthest from its centre.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; rime ice, crevasses and quick melt-freeze cycles.
destinations.weather: Equatorial: no real seasons, but drier windows; altitude is the challenge.

tours.name: Cotopaxi
tours.note: Midnight start from the hut; summit at dawn.

tours.name: Chimborazo
tours.note: A long, cold, high climb.

destinations.name: Mount Ararat
destinations.crowdNote: Very few ski parties.
destinations.pitch: Ski the 5,137 m volcano where Noah's Ark is said to rest, with mule support to camp and views into Iran and Armenia.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; open, mostly moderate slopes.
destinations.weather: Cold, windy summit days; best snow March–April.
destinations.advisory: Ararat is a military border zone: a climbing permit through a licensed Turkish agency is required and takes weeks. Check your government's advice for eastern Türkiye.

children.name: Doğubayazıt
children.note: Town at the foot, and the base for climbs.

tours.name: South route
tours.note: About a week, with two high camps.

destinations.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
destinations.crowdNote: Remote; you will see your own team.
destinations.pitch: Ski onto the largest ice field outside the poles, under the east faces of Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre.
destinations.avalanche: No forecast service; glacier travel and storm-proof camping essential.
destinations.weather: Infamous wind and storms; good-weather windows are short and precious.

children.name: El Chaltén
children.note: Trekking town at the foot of Fitz Roy.

children.name: Paso Marconi
children.note: The usual way onto the ice.

tours.name: Marconi–Paso del Viento loop
tours.note: About a week to ten days behind Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre.

destinations.name: Greenland Ice Cap Crossing
destinations.crowdNote: A few dozen teams a year.
destinations.pitch: The classic polar journey: about 550 km and four weeks pulling a sled across the ice cap, coast to coast.
destinations.avalanche: Not an avalanche trip; crevasses near the coasts, piteraq storms and cold injury are the risks.
destinations.weather: −30 °C nights in spring; katabatic storms.

children.name: DYE-2
children.note: Abandoned Cold War radar station on the ice.

children.name: Point 660 (Kangerlussuaq)
children.note: Western edge of the ice, the usual finish.

destinations.name: Vatnajökull Crossing
destinations.crowdNote: A few guided groups each spring.
destinations.pitch: Europe's largest ice cap on skis: a week-plus pulling sleds over volcanoes buried under the ice.
destinations.avalanche: Low avalanche exposure; crevasses, whiteout and storms are the risks.
destinations.weather: Fast-moving Atlantic storms; long spring days.

children.name: Grímsvötn
children.note: Active volcano under the ice, with a hut on its rim.

children.name: Hvannadalshnúkur
children.note: Iceland's highest peak, a big spring ski ascent.

children.name: Jökulsárlón
children.note: Glacier lagoon on the southern edge.

tours.name: Hvannadalshnúkur
tours.note: About 2,000 m of climbing from near sea level.

tours.name: Vatnajökull crossing
tours.note: A week or more pulling sleds over the ice cap.

destinations.name: Sarek
destinations.crowdNote: Roadless and hutless: true solitude.
destinations.pitch: Sweden's wildest park: no huts, no roads, no trails, a week of tent and sled touring among glaciated peaks.
destinations.avalanche: Swedish avalanche forecasts cover nearby areas; steep valley sides.
destinations.weather: Cold and windy; March–April brings light and stable days.

children.name: Kvikkjokk
children.note: Southern starting point.

children.name: Ritsem
children.note: Northern starting point.

children.name: Saltoluokta
children.note: STF mountain station on the eastern side.

tours.name: Sarek crossing via Rapadalen
tours.note: A week or more with a pulk, through the park's great valley.

children.name: Jikepulin (Hemu)
children.note: 1,466 m vertical; Freeride World Tour qualifier venue.

children.name: Koktokay
children.note: Big, steep resort near Fuyun.

children.name: Jiangjunshan
children.note: Town hill above Altay city; ancient ski rock art nearby.

destinations.name: Altay: Jikepulin-Hemu
destinations.crowdNote: Growing fast domestically; still quiet midweek.
destinations.pitch: Bone-dry powder in the hills that claim to be the birthplace of skiing, beside a Tuvan log-cabin village.
destinations.avalanche: Resort patrol closes high-risk zones; no public regional forecast.
destinations.weather: Very cold (−20 °C common); light, cold smoke snow.
destinations.advisory: Xinjiang has pervasive police checkpoints and surveillance; border areas (including Hemu/Kanas and the Pamir) need extra permits, and some travellers also weigh the region's human-rights situation. Check your government's travel advice.

destinations.name: Erciyes & Cappadocia
destinations.crowdNote: Busy on Turkish holidays only.
destinations.pitch: Ski an extinct 3,917 m volcano by day and sleep in a Cappadocian cave hotel among the balloons.
destinations.avalanche: Resort controlled; off-piste on open volcano slopes.
destinations.weather: Sunny, dry continental winters.

children.name: Erciyes ski resort
children.note: Modern lifts on the volcano's flanks.

children.name: Amirsoy
children.note: Modern resort opened 2019.

children.name: Chimgan & Beldersay
children.note: Soviet-era lifts; heli-ski base.

destinations.name: Amirsoy & Chimgan
destinations.crowdNote: Weekend crowds from Tashkent; quiet midweek.
destinations.pitch: New lifts and old Soviet runs in the Tian Shan, 90 minutes from Tashkent and a train ride from Samarkand.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast; off-piste and heli days with local guides.
destinations.weather: Continental, sunny; short season.

destinations.name: Popova Šapka Cat Skiing
destinations.crowdNote: Small groups, big terrain.
destinations.pitch: Europe's oldest cat-skiing operation, in the wild Šar Mountains above a small Balkan resort.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast; operators manage terrain.
destinations.weather: Balkan winter: storms from the Adriatic, then sun.

children.name: Popova Šapka
children.note: Small resort and the cat-skiing base.

children.name: Titov Vrv
children.note: Highest peak of the Macedonian Šar, a ski-touring objective.

children.name: Bansko ski area
children.note: 75 km of pistes; the backup for stormy days.

children.name: Vihren hut
children.note: Hut below Vihren's marble faces.

children.name: Banderitsa hut
children.note: Hut in the cirques above Bansko.

destinations.name: Pirin & Bansko
destinations.crowdNote: Bansko is lively; the tours are quiet.
destinations.pitch: Alpine limestone peaks up to 2,914 m Vihren above a cheap, lively resort town: tour by day, lifts as backup.
destinations.avalanche: Bulgarian mountain rescue publishes avalanche info; marble and limestone slabs.
destinations.weather: Mediterranean-influenced: big snows, then sunny spells.

tours.name: Vihren (2,914 m)
tours.note: The highest peak in the Pirin, with steep gullies.

tours.name: Banderitsa cirques
tours.note: Wide, open bowls above the hut.

destinations.name: Făgăraș & Bucegi (Carpathians)
destinations.crowdNote: A small local touring scene.
destinations.pitch: The highest Carpathians: a lake you reach by cable car in winter, an ice hotel, and steep alpine cirques that few foreign skiers know.
destinations.avalanche: Continental snowpack with wind slabs and cornices. Romania's national meteorology service publishes avalanche bulletins.
destinations.weather: Cold and windy, with heavy snow in some winters.

children.name: Bâlea Lac
children.note: Frozen lake reached by cable car, with steep cirques around.

children.name: Sinaia
children.note: Ski area and town below the Bucegi plateau.

children.name: Bucegi plateau
children.note: High plateau with easy touring and steep valleys on its edge.

tours.name: Bâlea Lac cirques
tours.note: Steep, open lines around the lake.

children.name: Kanin – Sella Nevea
children.note: Cross-border lift access to high karst terrain.

children.name: Triglav traverse
children.note: Slovenia's highest peak, a serious spring objective.

children.name: Vogel
children.note: Small ski area above Lake Bohinj, with plateau touring.

destinations.name: Julian Alps (Kanin & Triglav)
destinations.crowdNote: Busy weekends with locals.
destinations.pitch: Limestone karst peaks above emerald rivers: day tours from Kanin's lifts and a hut traverse around Triglav.
destinations.avalanche: Slovenian forecast (ARSO); limestone gullies and cornices.
destinations.weather: Big Adriatic storms; sunny clear spells.

tours.name: Triglav (2,864 m)
tours.note: Slovenia's national peak, in spring.

tours.name: Kanin plateau
tours.note: Karst touring from the top of the lifts.

destinations.name: Gran Sasso & Majella (Abruzzo)
destinations.crowdNote: Romans and locals on weekends; quiet midweek.
destinations.pitch: The highest mountains in the Apennines, two hours from Rome, with views to the Adriatic and an Arctic-looking plateau.
destinations.avalanche: Mediterranean snowpack with wind slabs and big cornices. Meteomont forecasts the Apennines.
destinations.weather: Storms from the Balkans can bring very heavy snow; strong winds.

children.name: Campo Imperatore
children.note: High plateau with a small ski area and huge touring terrain.

children.name: Corno Grande
children.note: Highest peak of the Apennines, with steep gullies.

children.name: Majella (Monte Amaro)
children.note: Wide, open massif to the south-east.

children.name: Roccaraso
children.note: Biggest ski area in the southern Apennines.

tours.name: Corno Grande
tours.note: The highest peak of the Apennines.

tours.name: Monte Amaro
tours.note: Long, open tour on the Majella.

destinations.name: Corsica: Alta Strada
destinations.crowdNote: A few guided groups per season.
destinations.pitch: The GR20 on skis: a week-long haute route along the granite spine of a Mediterranean island, with sea views.
destinations.avalanche: Météo-France bulletin for Corsica; variable cover year to year.
destinations.weather: Snow comes and goes fast; March is usually best.

children.name: Monte Cinto
children.note: Corsica's highest peak, usually toured from Haut Asco.

children.name: Haut Asco
children.note: Valley head in the north, start for Monte Cinto.

children.name: Vizzavona
children.note: Central pass and start for Monte d'Oro.

tours.name: Alta Strada traverse
tours.note: About a week along the island's spine, roughly following the GR20.

tours.name: Monte Cinto
tours.note: Long climb from Haut Asco to Corsica's highest summit.

tours.name: Monte d'Oro
tours.note: Steep, striking peak above Vizzavona.

destinations.name: Valle Maira
destinations.crowdNote: Popular with Europeans, but spread across hundreds of tours.
destinations.pitch: An Occitan valley with no lifts and hundreds of mapped tours, stone hamlets and some of the best food in the Alps.
destinations.avalanche: Southwestern Alps: often thin, faceted snowpack with persistent layers; the Piedmont regional bulletin (Arpa Piemonte) forecasts the valley.
destinations.weather: Southern Alps: sunnier than the north side, snow from Mediterranean storms.

children.name: Chiappera
children.note: Hamlet at the head of the valley, under the Rocca Provenzale.

children.name: Acceglio
children.note: Upper-valley village and touring base.

children.name: Monte Chersogno
children.note: Big, open pyramid and a classic tour.

tours.name: Monte Chersogno
tours.note: A classic, big open summit.

tours.name: Rocca la Marchisa
tours.note: A popular summit in the upper valley.

destinations.name: Mercantour (Maritime Alps)
destinations.crowdNote: Quiet outside the two resorts.
destinations.pitch: Ski in the morning, Mediterranean in the afternoon: the southernmost Alps, with big storms from the sea and wild touring.
destinations.avalanche: Mediterranean snowpack, often with weak layers in thin years. Météo-France forecasts the Mercantour massif.
destinations.weather: Big, irregular storms from the south-east (retour d'est); lots of sun.

children.name: Isola 2000
children.note: High resort near the Italian border.

children.name: Auron
children.note: Sunny, traditional village resort.

children.name: Madone de Fenestre
children.note: Trailhead and refuge below the Cime du Gélas.

children.name: Vallée des Merveilles
children.note: Valley of prehistoric rock carvings, with touring.

tours.name: Cime du Gélas (3,143 m)
tours.note: The highest peak of the range, a classic spring tour.

children.name: Naltar ski area
children.note: Small lift area run by the Pakistan Air Force; touring above.

children.name: Hunza (Karimabad)
children.note: Village base for touring in the valley.

destinations.name: Hunza & Naltar
destinations.crowdNote: Almost no foreign skiers.
destinations.pitch: Ski touring under 7,000 m Karakoram giants, with Hunza's apricot-orchard villages and legendary hospitality.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast; big terrain, local guides essential.
destinations.weather: Cold, dry winters; flights to Gilgit are weather-dependent.
destinations.advisory: Several governments advise against travel to parts of Pakistan; Gilgit-Baltistan is generally treated differently from border regions. Check your government's current advice and use a registered local operator.

destinations.name: Altai Tavan Bogd
destinations.crowdNote: Kazakh herders and eagle hunters; few skiers.
destinations.pitch: Yurt-based ski touring on Mongolia's highest glaciers, hosted by Kazakh eagle-hunting families.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast service: cold, thin, wind-affected snowpack; glaciers and crevasses. Expedition-style, guided only.
destinations.weather: Brutally cold in winter; spring is the touring season.

children.name: Potanin glacier base camp
children.note: Ger camp on Mongolia's largest glacier.

children.name: Khüiten Peak
children.note: Mongolia's highest peak, on the border.

tours.name: Khüiten Peak
tours.note: Glacier climb to Mongolia's highest point.

destinations.name: Manali Heli (Himachal)
destinations.crowdNote: One operator, small groups.
destinations.pitch: Long-running heli skiing in the Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges, with 1,000 m-plus runs from Himalayan ridges.
destinations.avalanche: No public forecast: Himalayan wind and storm slabs on big terrain. The heli operator manages avalanche risk.
destinations.weather: Storms from the west, then clear cold spells.

children.name: Solang
children.note: Small lift-served area north of Manali.

destinations.name: Mount Fuji (spring)
destinations.crowdNote: A few dozen skiers on good May weekends.
destinations.pitch: Ski Japan's sacred volcano from the crater rim in late spring: a 1,500 m run with the whole country at your feet.
destinations.avalanche: Slush avalanches and hard icy slopes; falls are the main danger. Climbing plan required off-season.
destinations.weather: Wind and ice early; corn snow in May–June.

children.name: Fujinomiya 5th station
children.note: South-side start, once the road opens.

children.name: Subashiri 5th station
children.note: East-side start.

tours.name: Crater-rim descent
tours.note: Around 1,500 m from near the rim.

children.name: CairnGorm Mountain
children.note: Lift access to the plateau.

children.name: Glencoe Mountain
children.note: Steep, characterful ski area.

children.name: Nevis Range
children.note: Gondola to Aonach Mòr's freeride gullies.

children.name: Glenshee
children.note: The biggest Scottish ski area.

children.name: The Lecht
children.note: Small, family-friendly area.

children.name: Cairngorm plateau
children.note: Arctic-feeling plateau touring above CairnGorm Mountain.

children.name: Ben Nevis
children.note: The UK's highest peak, with steep north-face gullies.

destinations.name: Scottish Highlands (Cairngorms & Glencoe)
destinations.crowdNote: Busy with locals when it's good.
destinations.pitch: Wild, wind-scoured Highland plateaus and gullies, with whisky and bothies after; brilliant when it's on.
destinations.avalanche: Scottish Avalanche Information Service: cornices and wind slab.
destinations.weather: Famously fickle: storms, thaws and a few perfect days.

tours.name: Number Four Gully
tours.note: A classic ski descent on Ben Nevis.

tours.name: Cairngorm plateau tour
tours.note: Wide, Arctic-feeling terrain; navigation essential.

children.name: Bunny Flat · Avalanche Gulch
children.note: Main south-side trailhead for Avalanche Gulch and Horse Camp.

children.name: Brewer Creek · north side
children.note: Quieter north-east access to the Hotlum-Wintun route.

children.name: Lassen Peak
children.note: Volcano with good spring skiing in Lassen Volcanic National Park.

destinations.name: Mount Shasta
destinations.crowdNote: Avalanche Gulch is busy on spring weekends; other sides are quiet.
destinations.pitch: A lone 4,322 m volcano with 2,000 m spring corn runs on every side, plus Lassen's volcano park 90 minutes away.
destinations.avalanche: Mount Shasta Avalanche Center; ice and rockfall high up.
destinations.weather: Corn cycles from April; summit wind and lenticular clouds.

tours.name: Avalanche Gulch
tours.note: The standard south-side climb and descent.

tours.name: Hotlum-Wintun Ridge
tours.note: A quieter, long north-side ski route.

tours.name: Lassen Peak
tours.note: A shorter volcano tour from the park road.

children.name: Valhalla Range
children.note: Lodges in granite terrain near Nelson and the Slocan Valley.

children.name: Battle Range (Selkirks)
children.note: Wild, remote lodges in the northern Selkirks.

children.name: Kokanee & Kaslo area
children.note: Lodges and huts close to Nelson and Kaslo, including Kokanee Glacier Cabin.

children.name: Fairy Meadow (Adamants)
children.note: The Alpine Club of Canada's famous hut in the Adamant Range.
children.more: Booked by lottery; heli access from Golden or Revelstoke.

destinations.name: BC Backcountry Lodges (Selkirks & Kootenays)
destinations.crowdNote: One group per lodge, per week.
destinations.pitch: Fly in by helicopter to a timber lodge at treeline, then tour from the door for a week of Interior BC powder.
destinations.avalanche: Avalanche Canada; persistent weak layers are common.
destinations.weather: Cold interior storms, stable high-pressure spells.

destinations.name: Washington Pass (North Cascades)
destinations.crowdNote: Opening weekend of Hwy 20 is a party; quiet after.
destinations.pitch: Each spring the North Cascades Highway reopens onto a week's worth of granite couloirs and glacier lines.
destinations.avalanche: Cascade maritime: storm slabs in winter, then wet slides and cornices in spring. NWAC forecasts the area.
destinations.weather: Spring corn, with sun and storms in equal measure.

children.name: Washington Pass
children.note: The main access point, under Liberty Bell and the Early Winters Spires.

children.name: Silver Star Mountain
children.note: Big peak east of the pass, with a famous couloir.

children.name: Mazama
children.note: Small base town in the upper Methow Valley, home to North Cascades Heli.

tours.name: Birthday Tour
tours.note: A classic long loop linking passes and descents around Washington Pass.

tours.name: Early Winters Couloir
tours.note: Steep couloir on the Early Winters Spires.

tours.name: Silver Star Couloir
tours.note: Classic couloir on Silver Star Mountain.

destinations.name: Shames & Northwest BC (Terrace, Stewart)
destinations.crowdNote: A tiny local scene.
destinations.pitch: Deep coastal snow and a co-op ski hill in remote northwest BC, with some of the world's biggest heli-ski terrain further north.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime snowpack, very deep. Avalanche Canada's Northwest Coastal forecast covers the area.
destinations.weather: Very snowy and often cloudy; long storms off the Pacific.

children.name: Shames Mountain
children.note: Community co-op ski area with lift-accessed backcountry.

children.name: Bell 2 · Stewart (heli)
children.note: Remote lodges with huge heli-skiing tenures.

destinations.name: Vancouver Island (Mt Washington)
destinations.crowdNote: Island locals on weekends; quiet midweek.
destinations.pitch: Deep coastal snow on an island, with a big local resort, a community-run hill and Strathcona Park touring.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime snowpack, heavy and deep. Avalanche Canada forecasts Vancouver Island.
destinations.weather: Wet and windy; rain at lower elevations, deep snow up high.

children.name: Mount Washington
children.note: The island's main resort, with deep coastal snow.

children.name: Mount Cain
children.note: Small community-run hill in the island's north.

children.name: Paradise Meadows (Strathcona)
children.note: Trailhead into Strathcona Park and the Forbidden Plateau.

destinations.name: Vancouver North Shore
destinations.crowdNote: Busy evenings and weekends; a city crowd.
destinations.pitch: Three ski areas within sight of downtown Vancouver, with night skiing and short backcountry tours above the city.
destinations.avalanche: Coastal maritime snowpack, heavy and wet. Avalanche Canada's South Coast forecast covers the area.
destinations.weather: Wet and mild; rain at the base is common, snow up high.

children.name: Cypress Mountain
children.note: Biggest of the three; 2010 Olympic venue.

children.name: Grouse Mountain
children.note: Tram-access ski area with city views.

children.name: Mount Seymour
children.note: Smallest of the three, with easy backcountry access.

tours.name: Seymour's peaks: Pump and Tim Jones
